flavor.29: They smack beaks with others of their kind to communicate. The strength and number of hits tell each other how they feel.
flavor.30: Known for forming harmonious couples, this Pokémon is brought to wedding ceremonies as a good luck charm.
flavor.latest: They smack beaks with others of their kind to communicate. The strength and number of hits tell each other how they feel.

flavor.27: With its sharp fangs, it will bite anything. It did not originally live in Alola but was imported from another region.
flavor.28: It wanders around in a never-ending search for food. At dusk, it collapses from exhaustion and falls asleep on the spot.
flavor.29: Its stomach takes up most of its long torso. It’s a big eater, so the amount Trainers have to spend on its food is no laughing matter.
flavor.30: Although it will eat anything, it prefers fresh living things, so it marches down streets in search of prey.
flavor.latest: Its stomach takes up most of its long torso. It’s a big eater, so the amount Trainers have to spend on its food is no laughing matter.

flavor.27: When it finds a trace of its prey, it patiently stakes out the location...but it’s always snoozing by nightfall.
flavor.28: It adores having Rattata and Raticate for dinner, but as it’s diurnal, it never encounters them. This Pokémon boasts incredible patience.
flavor.29: Although it wasn’t originally found in Alola, this Pokémon was brought over a long time ago when there was a huge Rattata outbreak.
flavor.30: Patient by nature, this Pokémon loses control of itself and pounces when it spots its favorite meal—Rattata!
flavor.latest: Although it wasn’t originally found in Alola, this Pokémon was brought over a long time ago when there was a huge Rattata outbreak.

flavor.27: Its strong jaw enables it to scrape trees and slurp out the sap. It normally lives underground.
flavor.28: They often gather near places frequented by electric Pokémon in order to avoid being attacked by bird Pokémon.
flavor.29: If you find its nest, you shouldn’t stick your hand inside. You’ll get bitten by an irritated Grubbin.
flavor.30: It spits a sticky thread to stop opponents in their tracks, and then it grabs them in its sharp, sturdy mandibles to take them down.
flavor.33: Its natural enemies, like Rookidee, may flee rather than risk getting caught in its large mandibles that can snap thick tree branches.
flavor.34: It uses its big jaws to dig nests into the forest floor, and it loves to feed on sweet tree sap.
flavor.latest: Its natural enemies, like Rookidee, may flee rather than risk getting caught in its large mandibles that can snap thick tree branches.

flavor.27: Its body is capable of storing electricity. On camping trips, people are grateful to have one around.
flavor.28: From the food it digests, it generates electricity, and it stores this energy in its electric sac.
flavor.29: It buries itself in fallen leaves and barely moves, munching away on humus. If you accidentally step on one, you’ll get a shock!
flavor.30: Its stout shell provides excellent defense from attacks. It uses electricity on persistent opponents.
flavor.33: While its durable shell protects it from attacks, Charjabug strikes at enemies with jolts of electricity discharged from the tips of its jaws.
flavor.34: Its digestive processes convert the leaves it eats into electricity. An electric sac in its belly stores the electricity for later use.
flavor.latest: While its durable shell protects it from attacks, Charjabug strikes at enemies with jolts of electricity discharged from the tips of its jaws.

flavor.27: It zips around, on sharp lookout for an opening. It concentrates electrical energy within its large jaws and uses it to zap its enemies.
flavor.28: It produces electricity via an electrical organ in its abdomen. It overwhelms bird Pokémon with shocking beams of electrical energy.
flavor.29: It has an organ that generates electricity in its abdomen. It concentrates energy in its strong jaws and fires off powerful jolts of electricity.
flavor.30: Vikavolt flusters opponents with acrobatic flying maneuvers. This creates an opening for it to deliver an electric beam attack.
flavor.33: It builds up electricity in its abdomen, focuses it through its jaws, and then fires the electricity off in concentrated beams.
flavor.34: If it carries a Charjabug to use as a spare battery, a flying Vikavolt can rapidly fire high-powered beams of electricity.
flavor.latest: It builds up electricity in its abdomen, focuses it through its jaws, and then fires the electricity off in concentrated beams.

flavor.27: While guarding its weak points with its pincers, it looks for an opening and unleashes punches. When it loses, it foams at the mouth and faints.
flavor.28: It punches so much, its pincers often come off from overuse, but they grow back quickly. What little meat they contain is rich and delicious.
flavor.29: Its hard pincers are well suited to both offense and defense. Fights between two Crabrawler are like boxing matches.
flavor.30: Crabrawler has been known to mistake Exeggutor for a coconut tree and climb it. The enraged Exeggutor shakes it off and stomps it.
flavor.latest: Its hard pincers are well suited to both offense and defense. Fights between two Crabrawler are like boxing matches.

flavor.27: It aimed for the top but got lost and ended up on a snowy mountain. Being forced to endure the cold, this Pokémon evolved and grew fur.
flavor.28: It just throws punches indiscriminately. In times of desperation, it can lop off its own pincers and fire them like rockets.
flavor.29: It stores coldness in its pincers and pummels its foes. It can even smash thick walls of ice to bits!
flavor.30: Before it stops to think, it just starts pummeling. There are records of its turning back avalanches with a flurry of punches.
flavor.latest: It stores coldness in its pincers and pummels its foes. It can even smash thick walls of ice to bits!

flavor.27: It beats its wings together to create fire. As it moves in the steps of its beautiful dance, it bathes opponents in intense flames.
flavor.28: This Oricorio has sipped red nectar. Its passionate dance moves cause its enemies to combust in both body and mind.
flavor.29: It wins the hearts of its enemies with its passionate dancing and then uses the opening it creates to burn them up with blazing flames.
flavor.30: This Oricorio has drunk red nectar. If its Trainer gives the wrong order, this passionate Pokémon becomes fiercely angry.
flavor.latest: It wins the hearts of its enemies with its passionate dancing and then uses the opening it creates to burn them up with blazing flames.

flavor.27: It feeds on the nectar and pollen of flowers. Because it’s able to sense auras, it can identify which flowers are about to bloom.
flavor.28: Myriads of Cutiefly flutter above the heads of people who have auras resembling those of flowers.
flavor.29: Nectar and pollen are its favorite fare. In fields of flowers, it gets into skirmishes with Butterfree over food.
flavor.30: Cutiefly can pick up the auras of living things. It skillfully reads those auras to predict its foes’ movements and make fools of them.
flavor.33: Nectar and pollen are its favorite fare. You can find Cutiefly hovering around Gossifleur, trying to get some of Gossifleur’s pollen.
flavor.34: An opponent’s aura can tell Cutiefly what that opponent’s next move will be. Then Cutiefly can glide around the attack and strike back.
flavor.latest: Nectar and pollen are its favorite fare. You can find Cutiefly hovering around Gossifleur, trying to get some of Gossifleur’s pollen.

flavor.27: It rolls up pollen into puffs. It makes many different varieties, some used as food and others used in battle.
flavor.28: Some of Ribombee’s pollen puffs are highly nutritious. They are sometimes sold as supplements.
flavor.29: Rain makes pollen damp, so Ribombee hates rain. When it sees ominous clouds, it finds a hollow in a tree, where it waits stock-still.
flavor.30: It can predict the weather from moisture levels and wind direction. Ribombee only reveals itself when there are a few clear days in a row.
flavor.33: It makes pollen puffs from pollen and nectar. The puffs’ effects depend on the type of ingredients and how much of each one is used.
flavor.34: Ribombee absolutely hate getting wet or rained on. In the cloudy Galar region, they are very seldom seen.
flavor.latest: It makes pollen puffs from pollen and nectar. The puffs’ effects depend on the type of ingredients and how much of each one is used.

flavor.27: It’s considered to be a good Pokémon for beginners because of its friendliness, but its disposition grows rougher as it grows up.
flavor.28: This Pokémon has lived with people since times long ago. It can sense when its Trainer is in the dumps and will stick close by its Trainer’s side.
flavor.29: As they develop, their disposition grows more violent and aggressive. Many Trainers find them too much to handle and abandon them.
flavor.30: When it rubs the rocks on its neck against you, that’s proof of its love for you. However, the rocks are sharp, so the gesture is quite painful!
flavor.33: This Pokémon can bond very strongly with its Trainer, but it also has a habit of biting. Raising a Rockruff for a long time can be challenging.
flavor.34: This Pokémon intimidates opponents by striking the ground with the rocks on its neck. The moment an opponent flinches, Rockruff attacks.
flavor.latest: This Pokémon can bond very strongly with its Trainer, but it also has a habit of biting. Raising a Rockruff for a long time can be challenging.

flavor.27: Its quick movements confuse its enemies. Well equipped with claws and fangs, it also uses the sharp rocks in its mane as weapons.
flavor.28: When properly raised from a young age, it will become a trustworthy partner that will absolutely never betray its Trainer.
flavor.29: The sharp rocks in its mane can cut like knives. Lycanroc wears its prey down by degrees before finishing them off.
flavor.30: The rocks in its mane are sharper than a knife. Fragments that break off are treasured as good luck charms.
flavor.33: This Lycanroc is calm and cautious. The rocks jutting from its mane are razor sharp.
flavor.34: With swift movements, this Pokémon gradually backs its prey into a corner. Lycanroc’s fangs are always aimed toward opponents’ weak spots.
flavor.latest: This Lycanroc is calm and cautious. The rocks jutting from its mane are razor sharp.

flavor.27: When it’s in trouble, its eyes moisten and begin to shine. The shining light attracts its comrades, and they stand together against their enemies.
flavor.28: It’s awfully weak and notably tasty, so everyone is always out to get it. As it happens, anyone trying to bully it receives a painful lesson.
flavor.29: They’re weak, so they move in schools. However, they can also often be seen all alone, having strayed from the school.
flavor.30: When it’s in a jam, its shining eyes attract others of its kind. The light from its eyes is visible almost 25 miles away.
flavor.33: Individually, they’re incredibly weak. It’s by gathering up into schools that they’re able to confront opponents.
flavor.34: When it senses danger, its eyes tear up. The sparkle of its tears signals other Wishiwashi to gather.
flavor.latest: Individually, they’re incredibly weak. It’s by gathering up into schools that they’re able to confront opponents.

flavor.27: It plunges the poison spike on its head into its prey. When the prey has weakened, Mareanie deals the finishing blow with its 10 tentacles.
flavor.28: It’s found crawling on beaches and seafloors. The coral that grows on Corsola’s head is as good as a five-star banquet to this Pokémon.
flavor.29: They eat Corsola branches, so Mareanie are hated by craftsmen who work with Corsola branches that have naturally fallen off.
flavor.30: Aside from its head, its body parts regenerate quickly if they’re cut off. After a good night’s sleep, Mareanie is back to normal.
flavor.33: The first symptom of its sting is numbness. The next is an itching sensation so intense that it’s impossible to resist the urge to claw at your skin.
flavor.34: Unlike their Alolan counterparts, the Mareanie of the Galar region have not yet figured out that the branches of Corsola are delicious.
flavor.latest: The first symptom of its sting is numbness. The next is an itching sensation so intense that it’s impossible to resist the urge to claw at your skin.

flavor.27: Toxapex crawls along the ocean floor on its 12 legs. It leaves a trail of Corsola bits scattered in its wake.
flavor.28: Those attacked by Toxapex’s poison will suffer intense pain for three days and three nights. Post-recovery, there will be some aftereffects.
flavor.29: To attack, this Pokémon sends toxic spikes flying at its enemies. Ones that come close get mown down by the claws on its feet.
flavor.30: With its 12 legs, it creates a dome to shelter within. The flow of the tides doesn’t affect Toxapex in there, so it’s very comfortable.
flavor.33: To survive in the cold waters of Galar, this Pokémon forms a dome with its legs, enclosing its body so it can capture its own body heat.
flavor.34: Within the poison sac in its body is a poison so toxic that Pokémon as large as Wailord will still be suffering three days after it first takes effect.
flavor.latest: To survive in the cold waters of Galar, this Pokémon forms a dome with its legs, enclosing its body so it can capture its own body heat.

flavor.27: The mud stuck to Mudbray’s hooves enhances its grip and its powerful running gait.
flavor.28: It has a stubborn, individualistic disposition. Eating dirt, making mud, and playing in the mire all form part of its daily routine.
flavor.29: It loves playing in the mud. If it isn’t showered with mud on a daily basis, it gets stressed out and stops listening to its Trainer.
flavor.30: Possessing mighty power, Mudbray can be loaded with 50 times its own body weight and will be totally fine.
flavor.33: Loads weighing up to 50 times as much as its own body weight pose no issue for this Pokémon. It’s skilled at making use of mud.
flavor.34: It eats dirt to create mud and smears this mud all over its feet, giving them the grip needed to walk on rough terrain without slipping.
flavor.latest: Loads weighing up to 50 times as much as its own body weight pose no issue for this Pokémon. It’s skilled at making use of mud.

flavor.27: It spits a mud that provides resistance to both wind and rain, so the walls of old houses were often coated with it.
flavor.28: Its heavy, mud-covered kicks are its best means of attack, and it can reduce large trucks to scrap without breaking a sweat.
flavor.29: It remains calm and unmoving no matter the situation. It mixes dirt with the saliva in its mouth to make a special kind of mud.
flavor.30: It can trudge mountain roads without rest for three days and three nights, all the while dragging a 10-ton load.
flavor.33: Mud that hardens around a Mudsdale’s legs sets harder than stone. It’s so hard that it allows this Pokémon to scrap a truck with a single kick.
flavor.34: Mudsdale has so much stamina that it could carry over 10 tons across the Galar region without rest or sleep.
flavor.latest: Mud that hardens around a Mudsdale’s legs sets harder than stone. It’s so hard that it allows this Pokémon to scrap a truck with a single kick.

flavor.27: It crawls onto the land in search of food. Its water bubble allows it to breathe and protects its soft head.
flavor.28: When it comes across enemies or potential prey, this Pokémon smashes its water-bubble-covered head into them.
flavor.29: When two Dewpider meet, they display their water bubbles to each other. Then the one with the smaller bubble gets out of the other’s way.
flavor.30: It can only breathe oxygen that has dissolved in water, so it wears a water bubble on its head when it walks around on land.
flavor.33: It forms a water bubble at the rear of its body and then covers its head with it. Meeting another Dewpider means comparing water-bubble sizes.
flavor.34: Dewpider normally lives underwater. When it comes onto land in search of food, it takes water with it in the form of a bubble on its head.
flavor.latest: It forms a water bubble at the rear of its body and then covers its head with it. Meeting another Dewpider means comparing water-bubble sizes.

flavor.27: It delivers headbutts with the water bubble on its head. Small Pokémon get sucked into the bubble, where they drown.
flavor.28: Despite what its appearance suggests, it cares for others. If it finds vulnerable, weak Pokémon, it protectively brings them into its water bubble.
flavor.29: It usually passes its time in the water. When its belly is full, it stores its subdued prey in the water bubble on its head.
flavor.30: It has a habit of storing things it values in its water bubble. If its Trainer doesn’t watch out, Araquanid will try to put them in its bubble!
flavor.33: It launches water bubbles with its legs, drowning prey within the bubbles. This Pokémon can then take its time to savor its meal.
flavor.34: It acts as a caretaker for Dewpider, putting them inside its bubble and letting them eat any leftover food.
flavor.latest: It launches water bubbles with its legs, drowning prey within the bubbles. This Pokémon can then take its time to savor its meal.

flavor.27: During the day, it sleeps and soaks up light. When night falls, it walks around looking for a safer place to sleep.
flavor.28: They give off a sweet and refreshing scent. Cutiefly often gather near the tall grass where Fomantis are hiding.
flavor.29: When the sun rises, Fomantis spreads its four leaves and bathes in the sunlight. The tip of its head has a pleasant aroma.
flavor.30: It loves the sunshine. When it basks in the sunlight regularly, it grows up with vivid coloration.
flavor.33: When bathed in sunlight, this Pokémon emits a pleasantly sweet scent, which causes bug Pokémon to gather around it.
flavor.34: During the day, Fomantis basks in sunlight and sleeps peacefully. It wakes and moves around at night.
flavor.latest: When bathed in sunlight, this Pokémon emits a pleasantly sweet scent, which causes bug Pokémon to gather around it.

flavor.27: It requires a lot of effort to maintain Lurantis’s vivid coloring, but some collectors enjoy this work and treat it as their hobby.
flavor.28: It fires beams from its sickle-shaped petals. These beams are powerful enough to cleave through thick metal plates.
flavor.29: For self-protection, it pretends to be a bug Pokémon. Both of its arms bear keen-edged petals.
flavor.30: As it slashes into its enemies, it looks like it’s dancing. Its elegant appearance has led some to call it the most glamorous Grass Pokémon.
flavor.33: This Pokémon resembles a beautiful flower. A properly raised Lurantis will have gorgeous, brilliant colors.
flavor.34: The petals on this Pokémon’s arms are thin and super sharp, and they can fire laser beams if Lurantis gathers light first.
flavor.latest: This Pokémon resembles a beautiful flower. A properly raised Lurantis will have gorgeous, brilliant colors.

flavor.27: It scatters spores that flicker and glow. Anyone seeing these lights falls into a deep slumber.
flavor.28: As it drowses the day away, it nourishes itself by sucking from tree roots. It wakens at the fall of night, wandering off in search of a new tree.
flavor.29: It scatters its shining spores around itself. Even though they’re dangerous, nighttime tours of forests where Morelull live are popular.
flavor.30: It likes damp dark places. When night falls, the spores filling the caps of its mushrooms glow.
flavor.33: Pokémon living in the forest eat the delicious caps on Morelull’s head. The caps regrow overnight.
flavor.34: Morelull live in forests that stay dark even during the day. They scatter flickering spores that put enemies to sleep.
flavor.latest: Pokémon living in the forest eat the delicious caps on Morelull’s head. The caps regrow overnight.

flavor.27: Forests where Shiinotic live are treacherous to enter at night. People confused by its strange lights can never find their way home again.
flavor.28: It emits flickering spores that cause drowsiness. When its prey succumb to sleep, this Pokémon feeds on them by sucking in their energy.
flavor.29: It puts its prey to sleep and siphons off their vitality through the tip of its arms. If one of its kind is weakened, it helps by sending it vitality.
flavor.30: When it starts fighting for territory with Parasect, the entire area gets completely coated in spores!
flavor.33: Its flickering spores lure in prey and put them to sleep. Once this Pokémon has its prey snoozing, it drains their vitality with its fingertips.
flavor.34: If you see a light deep in a forest at night, don’t go near. Shiinotic will make you fall fast asleep.
flavor.latest: Its flickering spores lure in prey and put them to sleep. Once this Pokémon has its prey snoozing, it drains their vitality with its fingertips.

flavor.27: It burns its bodily fluids to create a poisonous gas. When its enemies become disoriented from inhaling the gas, it attacks them.
flavor.28: Volcanoes or dry, craggy places are its home. It emanates a sweet-smelling poisonous gas that attracts bug Pokémon, then attacks them.
flavor.29: The males will do whatever the females tell them. They give the females most of their food. Due to malnutrition, the males can’t evolve.
flavor.30: It weakens opponents and sends them reeling with its poisonous gas. Salandit doesn’t deal well with Spinda, since it’s always reeling.
flavor.33: Its venom sacs produce a fluid that this Pokémon then heats up with the flame in its tail. This process creates Salandit’s poisonous gas.
flavor.34: This sneaky Pokémon will slink behind its prey and immobilize it with poisonous gas before the prey even realizes Salandit is there.
flavor.latest: Its venom sacs produce a fluid that this Pokémon then heats up with the flame in its tail. This process creates Salandit’s poisonous gas.

flavor.27: For some reason, only females have been found. It creates a reverse harem of male Salandit that it lives with.
flavor.28: Filled with pheromones, its poisonous gas can be diluted to use in the production of luscious perfumes.
flavor.29: Salazzle lives deep in caves and forces the Salandit it has attracted with its pheromones to serve it.
flavor.30: It punishes Salandit that couldn’t bring it food with a fierce slap of its flame-spewing palm.
flavor.33: Only female Salazzle exist. They emit a gas laden with pheromones to captivate male Salandit.
flavor.34: The winner of competitions between Salazzle is decided by which one has the most male Salandit with it.
flavor.latest: Only female Salazzle exist. They emit a gas laden with pheromones to captivate male Salandit.

flavor.27: Despite its adorable appearance, when it gets angry and flails about, its arms and legs could knock a pro wrestler sprawling.
flavor.28: A touch from anyone except a known friend sends it into a surging frenzy. It’s an incredibly dangerous Pokémon.
flavor.29: It boasts power enough to split large trees in half. The organ on its rear releases an odor that it uses to communicate with others of its kind.
flavor.30: Stufful hates to be hugged or touched in any way. It will squirm, thrash, and resist with amazing power.
flavor.33: Its fluffy fur is a delight to pet, but carelessly reaching out to touch this Pokémon could result in painful retaliation.
flavor.34: The way it protects itself by flailing its arms may be an adorable sight, but stay well away. This is flailing that can snap thick tree trunks.
flavor.latest: Its fluffy fur is a delight to pet, but carelessly reaching out to touch this Pokémon could result in painful retaliation.

flavor.27: This immensely dangerous Pokémon possesses overwhelming physical strength. Its habitat is generally off-limits.
flavor.28: This Pokémon has the habit of hugging its companions. Many Trainers have left this world after their spines were squashed by its hug.
flavor.29: It waves its hands wildly in intimidation and warning. Life is over for anyone who doesn’t run away as fast as possible.
flavor.30: It boasts tremendous physical strength. Many people call it the most dangerous Pokémon in the Alola region.
flavor.33: Once it accepts you as a friend, it tries to show its affection with a hug. Letting it do that is dangerous—it could easily shatter your bones.
flavor.34: The moves it uses to take down its prey would make a martial artist jealous. It tucks subdued prey under its arms to carry them to its nest.
flavor.latest: Once it accepts you as a friend, it tries to show its affection with a hug. Letting it do that is dangerous—it could easily shatter your bones.

flavor.27: A delectable aroma pours from its body. They are often swallowed whole by Toucannon lured by that wafting deliciousness.
flavor.28: Although it’s too sugary for human consumption, Bounsweet’s sweat can be watered down into a juice with just the right amount of sweetness.
flavor.29: Because of its sweet, delicious aroma, bird Pokémon are always after it, but it’s not intelligent enough to care.
flavor.30: It tries to resist being swallowed by a bird Pokémon by spinning the sepals on its head. It’s usually a fruitless attempt.
flavor.33: Its body gives off a sweet, fruity scent that is extremely appetizing to bird Pokémon.
flavor.34: When under attack, it secretes a sweet and delicious sweat. The scent only calls more enemies to it.
flavor.latest: Its body gives off a sweet, fruity scent that is extremely appetizing to bird Pokémon.

flavor.27: The sepals on its head developed to protect its body. These are quite hard, so even if pecked by bird Pokémon, this Pokémon is totally fine.
flavor.28: This Pokémon is always bouncing around energetically. Other Pokémon are attracted by its lively appearance and pleasant aroma.
flavor.29: It’s protected by its hard sepals, so it plays with bird Pokémon without worry. They peck it relentlessly, but it doesn’t care.
flavor.30: It bounces around, swinging the sepals on its head with abandon. They’re quite painful when they smack you!
flavor.33: As it twirls like a dancer, a sweet smell spreads out around it. Anyone who inhales the scent will feel a surge of happiness.
flavor.34: Any Corvisquire that pecks at this Pokémon will be greeted with a smack from its sepals followed by a sharp kick.
flavor.latest: As it twirls like a dancer, a sweet smell spreads out around it. Anyone who inhales the scent will feel a surge of happiness.

flavor.27: Its long, striking legs aren’t just for show but to be used to kick with skill. In victory, it shows off by kicking the defeated, laughing boisterously.
flavor.28: A Pokémon known for the beauty of its well-shaped legs, it sometimes appears as a mascot in advertisements for beauty salons.
flavor.29: A master of grand and beautiful kicks, it can knock out even kickboxing champions with a single blow.
flavor.30: A Pokémon with an aggressive personality and a mastery of kicking, it cackles every time it kicks an opponent.
flavor.33: This feared Pokémon has long, slender legs and a cruel heart. It shows no mercy as it stomps on its opponents.
flavor.34: A kick from the hardened tips of this Pokémon’s legs leaves a wound in the opponent’s body and soul that will never heal.
flavor.latest: This feared Pokémon has long, slender legs and a cruel heart. It shows no mercy as it stomps on its opponents.

flavor.27: It attaches flowers to its highly nutritious vine. This revitalizes the flowers, and they give off an aromatic scent.
flavor.28: Baths prepared with the flowers from its vine have a relaxing effect, so this Pokémon is a hit with many people.
flavor.29: It stretches sticky vines out from its head and picks flowers to adorn itself with. When it doesn’t have any flowers, it feels uneasy.
flavor.30: It picks flowers and sticks them to its body with fluids it produces. The aroma that wafts from its petals has a healing effect.
flavor.33: Comfey picks flowers with its vine and decorates itself with them. For some reason, flowers won’t wither once they’re attached to a Comfey.
flavor.34: These Pokémon smell very nice. All Comfey wear different flowers, so each of these Pokémon has its own individual scent.
flavor.latest: Comfey picks flowers with its vine and decorates itself with them. For some reason, flowers won’t wither once they’re attached to a Comfey.

flavor.27: Known for its extreme intelligence, this Pokémon will look down on inexperienced Trainers, so it’s best suited to veteran Trainers.
flavor.28: Deep in the jungle, high in the lofty canopy, this Pokémon abides. On rare occasions, it shows up at the beach to match wits with Slowking.
flavor.29: It normally spends its time meditating in the treetops. It throws Poké Balls and gives other Pokémon orders as it pleases.
flavor.30: Oranguru don’t get along with each other, so they’re always engaging in battles of wits to decide which one is superior.
flavor.33: With waves of its fan—made from leaves and its own fur—Oranguru skillfully gives instructions to other Pokémon.
flavor.34: It knows the forest inside and out. If it comes across a wounded Pokémon, Oranguru will gather medicinal herbs to treat it.
flavor.latest: With waves of its fan—made from leaves and its own fur—Oranguru skillfully gives instructions to other Pokémon.

flavor.27: They form groups of roughly 20 individuals. Their mutual bond is remarkable—they will never let down a comrade.
flavor.28: They battle with hard berries for weapons. Their techniques are passed from the boss to the group, generation upon generation.
flavor.29: They use their saliva to stick leaves to their shoulders. You can tell what troop they belong to from the position of the leaves.
flavor.30: Berries are its weapons as well as the staple of its diet. The one that can throw a berry the farthest is the boss of the troop.
flavor.33: Displaying amazing teamwork, they follow the orders of their boss as they all help out in the search for their favorite berries.
flavor.34: Passimian live in groups of about 20, with each member performing an assigned role. Through cooperation, the group survives.
flavor.latest: Displaying amazing teamwork, they follow the orders of their boss as they all help out in the search for their favorite berries.

flavor.27: This Pokémon is a coward. As it desperately dashes off, the flailing of its many legs leaves a sparkling clean path in its wake.
flavor.28: Its habitat varies from beaches to seabeds. A natural scavenger, it will gleefully chow down on anything edible, no matter how rotten.
flavor.29: It will pick up anything it finds on the ground. Sometimes it finds coins, so Murkrow and Meowth will go after it.
flavor.30: An astonishingly cowardly Pokémon, Wimpod will whir its legs at high speeds to run away if anything comes near it.
flavor.33: It’s nature’s cleaner—it eats anything and everything, including garbage and rotten things. The ground near its nest is always clean.
flavor.34: Wimpod gather in swarms, constantly on the lookout for danger. They scatter the moment they detect an enemy’s presence.
flavor.latest: It’s nature’s cleaner—it eats anything and everything, including garbage and rotten things. The ground near its nest is always clean.

flavor.27: With a flashing slash of its giant sharp claws, it cleaves seawater—or even air—right in two.
flavor.28: It battles skillfully with its six arms, but spends most of its time peacefully meditating in caves deep beneath the sea.
flavor.29: The shell covering its body is as hard as diamond. This Pokémon will do anything it takes to win.
flavor.30: Its claws, which it can extend and retract at will, are its greatest weapons. Golisopod is sometimes accompanied by Wimpod.
flavor.33: It will do anything to win, taking advantage of every opening and finishing opponents off with the small claws on its front legs.
flavor.34: They live in sunken ships or in holes in the seabed. When Golisopod and Grapploct battle, the loser becomes the winner’s meal.
flavor.latest: It will do anything to win, taking advantage of every opening and finishing opponents off with the small claws on its front legs.

flavor.27: Born from a sand mound playfully built by a child, this Pokémon embodies the grudges of the departed.
flavor.28: It takes control of anyone who puts a hand in its mouth. And so it adds to the accumulation of its sand-mound body.
flavor.29: It likes the shovel on its head, so Sandygast will get serious and fight any children who come to take it back.
flavor.30: If you build sand mounds when you’re playing, destroy them before you go home, or they may get possessed and become Sandygast.
flavor.33: Grudges of the dead have possessed a mound of sand and become a Pokémon. Sandygast is fond of the shovel on its head.
flavor.34: Sandygast mainly inhabits beaches. It takes control of anyone who puts their hand into its mouth, forcing them to make its body bigger.
flavor.latest: Grudges of the dead have possessed a mound of sand and become a Pokémon. Sandygast is fond of the shovel on its head.

flavor.27: Possessed people controlled by this Pokémon transformed its sand mound into a castle. As it evolved, its power to curse grew ever stronger.
flavor.28: Buried beneath the castle are masses of dried-up bones from those whose vitality it has drained.
flavor.29: Each of its grains of sand has its own will. Palossand eats small Pokémon and siphons away their vital essence while they’re still alive.
flavor.30: Once it has whipped up a sandstorm to halt its opponents in their tracks, this terrifying Pokémon snatches away their vitality.
flavor.33: Palossand is known as the Beach Nightmare. It pulls its prey down into the sand by controlling the sand itself, and then it sucks out their souls.
flavor.34: This Pokémon lives on beaches, but it hates water. Palossand can’t maintain its castle-like shape if it gets drenched by a heavy rain.
flavor.latest: Palossand is known as the Beach Nightmare. It pulls its prey down into the sand by controlling the sand itself, and then it sucks out their souls.

flavor.27: It lives in shallow seas, such as areas near a beach. It can eject its internal organs, which it uses to engulf its prey or battle enemies.
flavor.28: These Pokémon line the beaches. The sticky mucous that covers their bodies can be used to soothe sunburned skin. How convenient!
flavor.29: The tradition known as Pyukumuku chucking started from the custom of throwing Pyukumuku back into the sea after they wash onshore.
flavor.30: Its entire body is covered in its own slime. If you accidentally step on one, you’ll slip, and it will get mad and smack you!
flavor.33: It lives in warm, shallow waters. If it encounters a foe, it will spit out its internal organs as a means to punch them.
flavor.34: It’s covered in a slime that keeps its skin moist, allowing it to stay on land for days without drying up.
flavor.latest: It lives in warm, shallow waters. If it encounters a foe, it will spit out its internal organs as a means to punch them.

flavor.27: The heavy control mask it wears suppresses its intrinsic capabilities. This Pokémon has some hidden special power.
flavor.28: Due to the danger that this synthetic Pokémon may go on a rampage, it wears a control mask to restrain its power.
flavor.29: A Pokémon weapon developed for a specific mission, it went berserk during an experiment, so it was cryogenically frozen.
flavor.30: There’s danger of its going on a rampage, so its true power is sealed away beneath its control mask.
flavor.33: Rumor has it that the theft of top-secret research notes led to a new instance of this Pokémon being created in the Galar region.
flavor.34: It was modeled after a mighty Pokémon of myth. The mask placed upon it limits its power in order to keep it under control.
flavor.latest: Rumor has it that the theft of top-secret research notes led to a new instance of this Pokémon being created in the Galar region.

flavor.27: Its trust in its partner is what awakens it. This Pokémon is capable of changing its type, a flexibility that is well displayed in battle.
flavor.28: Although its name was Type: Null at first, the boy who evolved it into this form gave it the name by which it is now known.
flavor.29: This is its form once it has awakened and evolved. Freed from its heavy mask, its speed is greatly increased.
flavor.30: Through the bond it formed with its Trainer, its will was strengthened, and it was able to destroy its control mask.
flavor.33: A solid bond of trust between this Pokémon and its Trainer awakened the strength hidden within Silvally. It can change its type at will.
flavor.34: The final factor needed to release this Pokémon’s true power was a strong bond with a Trainer it trusts.
flavor.latest: A solid bond of trust between this Pokémon and its Trainer awakened the strength hidden within Silvally. It can change its type at will.

flavor.27: Originally making its home in the ozone layer, it hurtles to the ground when the shell enclosing its body grows too heavy.
flavor.28: Strong impacts can knock it out of its shell. This Pokémon was born from mutated nanoparticles.
flavor.29: It lives in the ozone layer, where it becomes food for stronger Pokémon. When it tries to run away, it falls to the ground.
flavor.30: Although its outer shell is uncommonly durable, the shock of falling to the ground smashes the shell to smithereens.
flavor.latest: It lives in the ozone layer, where it becomes food for stronger Pokémon. When it tries to run away, it falls to the ground.

flavor.27: It is born asleep, and it dies asleep. All its movements are apparently no more than the results of it tossing and turning in its dreams.
flavor.28: The log it holds was given to it by its parents at birth. It has also been known to cling to the arm of a friendly Trainer.
flavor.29: It stays asleep from the moment it’s born. When it falls into a deep sleep, it stops moving altogether.
flavor.30: It remains asleep from birth to death as a result of the sedative properties of the leaves that form its diet.
flavor.latest: It stays asleep from the moment it’s born. When it falls into a deep sleep, it stops moving altogether.

flavor.27: The shell on its back is chemically unstable and explodes violently if struck. The hole in its stomach is its weak point.
flavor.28: It gushes fire and poisonous gases from its nostrils. Its dung is an explosive substance and can be put to various uses.
flavor.29: It lives in volcanoes and eats sulfur and other minerals. Materials from the food it eats form the basis of its explosive shell.
flavor.30: Its exploding shell poses a real danger but is sensitive to moisture. On rainy days, Turtonator takes silent refuge in caves.
flavor.33: Explosive substances coat the shell on its back. Enemies that dare attack it will be blown away by an immense detonation.
flavor.34: Eating sulfur in its volcanic habitat is what causes explosive compounds to develop in its shell. Its droppings are also dangerously explosive.
flavor.latest: Explosive substances coat the shell on its back. Enemies that dare attack it will be blown away by an immense detonation.

flavor.27: The spiny fur on its back is normally at rest. When this Pokémon becomes agitated, its fur stands on end and stabs into its attackers.
flavor.28: The long hairs on its back act as lightning rods. The bolts of lightning it attracts are stored as energy in its electric sac.
flavor.29: When it’s surprised or agitated, the 14 fur spikes on its back will stand up involuntarily.
flavor.30: Its capacity to produce electricity is somewhat limited, so it gets charged up by letting lightning strike it!
flavor.33: With the long hairs on its back, this Pokémon takes in electricity from other electric Pokémon. It stores what it absorbs in an electric sac.
flavor.34: When it’s in trouble, it curls up into a ball, makes its fur spikes stand on end, and then discharges electricity indiscriminately.
flavor.latest: With the long hairs on its back, this Pokémon takes in electricity from other electric Pokémon. It stores what it absorbs in an electric sac.

flavor.27: Its actual appearance is unknown. A scholar who saw what was under its rag was overwhelmed by terror and died from the shock.
flavor.28: A lonely Pokémon, it conceals its terrifying appearance beneath an old rag so it can get closer to people and other Pokémon.
flavor.29: Although it’s a quiet, lonely Pokémon, if you try to look at what’s under its rag, it will become agitated and resist violently.
flavor.30: A gust of wind revealed what hides under this Pokémon’s rag to a passing Trainer, who went home and died painfully that very night.
flavor.33: It wears a rag fashioned into a Pikachu costume in an effort to look less scary. Unfortunately, the costume only makes it creepier.
flavor.34: There was a scientist who peeked under Mimikyu’s old rag in the name of research. The scientist died of a mysterious disease.
flavor.latest: It wears a rag fashioned into a Pikachu costume in an effort to look less scary. Unfortunately, the costume only makes it creepier.

flavor.27: When it unleashes its psychic power from the protuberance on its head, the grating sound of grinding teeth echoes through the area.
flavor.28: It stuns its prey with psychokinesis and then grinds them to mush with its strong teeth. Even Shellder’s shell is no match for it.
flavor.29: It burrows beneath the sand, radiating psychic power from the protuberance on its head. It waits for prey as it surveys the area.
flavor.30: Its skin is thick enough to fend off Mareanie’s spikes. With its robust teeth, Bruxish crunches up the spikes and eats them.
flavor.latest: It burrows beneath the sand, radiating psychic power from the protuberance on its head. It waits for prey as it surveys the area.

flavor.27: It has a compassionate personality, but if it is angered, it completely destroys its surroundings with its intense breath.
flavor.28: This Pokémon is friendly to people and loves children most of all. It comes from deep in the mountains to play with children it likes in town.
flavor.29: If a child it has made friends with is bullied, Drampa will find the bully’s house and burn it to the ground.
flavor.30: It appears in towns and plays with the children. Drampa will protect kids when they’re in danger, so their moms don’t have to worry.
flavor.33: The mountains it calls home are nearly two miles in height. On rare occasions, it descends to play with the children living in the towns below.
flavor.34: Drampa is a kind and friendly Pokémon—up until it’s angered. When that happens, it stirs up a gale and flattens everything around.
flavor.latest: The mountains it calls home are nearly two miles in height. On rare occasions, it descends to play with the children living in the towns below.

flavor.27: Swinging its massive anchor, it can KO Wailord in a single blow. What appears to be green seaweed is actually its body.
flavor.28: The soul of seaweed adrift in the waves became reborn as this Pokémon. It maintains itself with new infusions of seabed detritus and seaweed.
flavor.29: It wraps its prey in green seaweed and sucks away their vitality. It only likes to go after big prey like Wailord.
flavor.30: Its chain-like green seaweed can stretch outward for hundreds of yards. For some reason, it gets along well with Skrelp.
flavor.33: After a piece of seaweed merged with debris from a sunken ship, it was reborn as this ghost Pokémon.
flavor.34: After lowering its anchor, it waits for its prey. It catches large Wailord and drains their life-force.
flavor.latest: After a piece of seaweed merged with debris from a sunken ship, it was reborn as this ghost Pokémon.

flavor.27: It expresses its feelings by smacking its scales. Metallic sounds echo through the tall mountains where Jangmo-o lives.
flavor.28: They live in mountains where no trace of humans can be detected. Jangmo-o grow little by little as they battle one another.
flavor.29: It smacks the scales on its head against rocks or against the ground to frighten its opponents. It can also contact its friends with these noises.
flavor.30: It will never show an enemy its back in battle. Ancient warriors liked Jangmo-o for its valiant disposition and made it one of their own.
flavor.33: They learn to fight by smashing their head scales together. The dueling strengthens both their skills and their spirits.
flavor.34: Jangmo-o strikes its scales to communicate with others of its kind. Its scales are actually fur that’s become as hard as metal.
flavor.latest: They learn to fight by smashing their head scales together. The dueling strengthens both their skills and their spirits.

flavor.27: It leaps at its prey with a courageous shout. Its scaly punches tear its opponents to shreds.
flavor.28: It sheds and regrows its scales on a continuous basis. The scales become harder and sharper each time they’re regrown.
flavor.29: It makes noise by clanging its scales together. When the rhythm has reached its peak, Hakamo-o attacks.
flavor.30: The scales it sheds can be molded and processed to make pots and pans. They conduct heat well, so they’re a popular item.
flavor.33: The scaleless, scarred parts of its body are signs of its strength. It shows them off to defeated opponents.
flavor.34: Before attacking its enemies, it clashes its scales together and roars. Its sharp claws shred the opposition.
flavor.latest: The scaleless, scarred parts of its body are signs of its strength. It shows them off to defeated opponents.

flavor.27: When it spots enemies, it threatens them by jingling the scales on its tail. Weak opponents will crack and flee in panic.
flavor.28: Its rigid scales function as offense and defense. In the past, its scales were processed and used to make weapons and other commodities.
flavor.29: When it howls after finishing off its prey, the metallic sounds of its celebrating comrades can be heard from all around.
flavor.30: It battles valiantly with its fists, which are armored in steel scales. Kommo-o specializes in uppercuts.
flavor.33: It clatters its tail scales to unnerve opponents. This Pokémon will battle only those who stand steadfast in the face of this display.
flavor.34: Certain ruins have paintings of ancient warriors wearing armor made of Kommo-o scales.
flavor.latest: It clatters its tail scales to unnerve opponents. This Pokémon will battle only those who stand steadfast in the face of this display.

flavor.27: This guardian deity of Melemele is brimming with curiosity. It summons thunderclouds and stores their lightning inside its body.
flavor.28: It confuses its enemies by flying too quickly for the eye to follow. It has a hair-trigger temper but forgets what made it angry an instant later.
flavor.29: Although it’s called a guardian deity, if a person or Pokémon puts it in a bad mood, it will become a malevolent deity and attack.
flavor.30: The lightning-wielding guardian deity of Melemele, Tapu Koko is brimming with curiosity and appears before people from time to time.
flavor.latest: Although it’s called a guardian deity, if a person or Pokémon puts it in a bad mood, it will become a malevolent deity and attack.

flavor.27: This guardian deity of Akala is guilelessly cruel. The fragrant aroma of flowers is the source of its energy.
flavor.28: As it flutters about, it scatters its strangely glowing scales. Touching them is said to restore good health on the spot.
flavor.29: It heals the wounds of people and Pokémon by sprinkling them with its sparkling scales. This guardian deity is worshiped on Akala.
flavor.30: Although called a guardian deity, Tapu Lele is devoid of guilt about its cruel disposition and can be described as nature incarnate.
flavor.latest: It heals the wounds of people and Pokémon by sprinkling them with its sparkling scales. This guardian deity is worshiped on Akala.

flavor.27: It pulls large trees up by the roots and swings them around. It causes vegetation to grow, and then it absorbs energy from the growth.
flavor.28: The guardian deity of Ula’ula is a lazy Pokémon. It commands plants to immobilize its foes and then deals them a savage blow with its horns.
flavor.29: Although it’s called a guardian deity, it’s violent enough to crush anyone it sees as an enemy.
flavor.30: It makes ringing sounds with its tail to let others know where it is, avoiding unneeded conflicts. This guardian deity of Ula’ula controls plants.
flavor.latest: Although it’s called a guardian deity, it’s violent enough to crush anyone it sees as an enemy.

flavor.27: The dense fog it creates brings the downfall and destruction of its confused enemies. Ocean currents are the source of its energy.
flavor.28: The guardian deity of Poni, it can control water. People say it can create pure water that will wash away any uncleanness.
flavor.29: This guardian deity of Poni Island manipulates water. Because it lives deep within a thick fog, it came to be both feared and revered.
flavor.30: Although it’s called a guardian deity, terrible calamities sometimes befall those who recklessly approach Tapu Fini.
flavor.latest: This guardian deity of Poni Island manipulates water. Because it lives deep within a thick fog, it came to be both feared and revered.

flavor.27: Its body is gaseous and frail. It slowly grows as it collects dust from the atmosphere.
flavor.28: In ages past, it was called the child of the stars. It’s said to be a Pokémon from another world, but no specific details are known.
flavor.29: Even though its helpless, gaseous body can be blown away by the slightest breeze, it doesn’t seem to care.
flavor.30: Whether or not it’s a Pokémon from this world is a mystery. When it’s in a jam, it warps away to a safe place to hide.
flavor.33: This Pokémon came from another universe. Its gaseous body is so light that even a gentle breeze can blow it away.
flavor.34: Cosmog is very curious but not very cautious, often placing itself in danger. If things start to look dicey, it teleports away.
flavor.latest: This Pokémon came from another universe. Its gaseous body is so light that even a gentle breeze can blow it away.

flavor.27: Motionless as if dead, its body is faintly warm to the touch. In the distant past, it was called the cocoon of the stars.
flavor.28: There’s something accumulating around the black core within its hard shell. People think this Pokémon may come from another world.
flavor.29: The king who ruled Alola in times of antiquity called it the “cocoon of the stars” and built an altar to worship it.
flavor.30: As it absorbs light, Cosmoem continues to grow. Its golden shell is surprisingly solid.
flavor.33: The absorption of starlight fuels this Pokémon’s growth. The shell that encases it is harder than any known material.
flavor.34: It sucks in dust from the air at an astounding rate, frantically building up energy within its core as preparation for evolution.
flavor.latest: The absorption of starlight fuels this Pokémon’s growth. The shell that encases it is harder than any known material.

flavor.27: It is said to live in another world. The intense light it radiates from the surface of its body can make the darkest of nights light up like midday.
flavor.28: This Pokémon is said to be a male evolution of Cosmog. At the activation of its third eye, it departs for another world.
flavor.29: Sometimes the result of its opening an Ultra Wormhole is that energy and life-forms from other worlds are called here to this world.
flavor.30: In writings from the distant past, it’s called by the name “the beast that devours the sun.”
flavor.33: When light radiates from its body, this Pokémon could almost appear to be the sun. It will dispel any darkness and light up the world.
flavor.34: Solgaleo was once known as the Beast That Devours the Sun. Energy in the form of light radiates boundlessly from it.
flavor.latest: When light radiates from its body, this Pokémon could almost appear to be the sun. It will dispel any darkness and light up the world.

flavor.27: It is said to be a female evolution of Cosmog. When its third eye activates, away it flies to another world.
flavor.28: Said to live in another world, this Pokémon devours light, drawing the moonless dark veil of night over the brightness of day.
flavor.29: Records of it exist in writings from long, long ago, where it was known by the name “the beast that calls the moon.”
flavor.30: It sometimes summons unknown powers and life-forms here to this world from holes that lead to other worlds.
flavor.33: Known as the Beast That Calls the Moon, this Pokémon lives by taking in any and all light and converting it into its own energy.
flavor.34: It steals the light from its surroundings and then becomes the full moon, showering its own light across the night sky.
flavor.latest: Known as the Beast That Calls the Moon, this Pokémon lives by taking in any and all light and converting it into its own energy.

flavor.27: One of several mysterious Ultra Beasts. People on the street report observing those infested by it suddenly becoming violent.
flavor.28: One of the Ultra Beasts. It’s unclear whether or not this Pokémon is sentient, but sometimes it can be observed behaving like a young girl.
flavor.29: A life-form from another world, it was dubbed a UB and is thought to produce a strong neurotoxin.
flavor.30: It appeared in this world from an Ultra Wormhole. Nihilego appears to be a parasite that lives by feeding on people and Pokémon.
flavor.latest: A life-form from another world, it was dubbed a UB and is thought to produce a strong neurotoxin.

flavor.27: This Ultra Beast appeared from another world. It shows off its body, but whether that display is a boast or a threat remains unclear.
flavor.28: A mysterious life-form called an Ultra Beast. Witnesses saw it pulverize a dump truck with a single punch.
flavor.29: Although it’s alien to this world and a danger here, it’s apparently a common organism in the world where it normally lives.
flavor.30: Buzzwole goes around showing off its abnormally swollen muscles. It is one kind of Ultra Beast.
flavor.latest: Although it’s alien to this world and a danger here, it’s apparently a common organism in the world where it normally lives.

flavor.27: One of the dangerous Ultra Beasts, it has been spotted running across the land at terrific speeds.
flavor.28: One of the Ultra Beasts. It refuses to touch anything, perhaps because it senses some uncleanness in this world.
flavor.29: A life-form that lives in another world, its body is thin and supple, but it also possesses great power.
flavor.30: Although it’s alien to this world and a danger here, it’s apparently a common organism in the world where it normally lives.
flavor.latest: A life-form that lives in another world, its body is thin and supple, but it also possesses great power.

flavor.27: One of the mysterious life-forms known as Ultra Beasts. Astonishing electric shocks emanate from its entire body, according to witnesses.
flavor.28: It appeared from the Ultra Wormhole. It raided a power plant, so people think it energizes itself with electricity.
flavor.29: Although it’s alien to this world and a danger here, it’s apparently a common organism in the world where it normally lives.
flavor.30: They’ve been dubbed Ultra Beasts. Some of them stand unmoving, like trees, with their arms and legs stuck into the ground.
flavor.latest: Although it’s alien to this world and a danger here, it’s apparently a common organism in the world where it normally lives.

flavor.27: It appeared from the Ultra Wormhole. Witnesses observed it flying across the sky at high speed.
flavor.28: One kind of Ultra Beast. Witnesses have seen it burn down a forest by expelling gas from its two arms.
flavor.29: One of the dangerous UBs, high energy readings can be detected coming from both of its huge arms.
flavor.30: Although it’s alien to this world and a danger here, it’s apparently a common organism in the world where it normally lives.
flavor.latest: One of the dangerous UBs, high energy readings can be detected coming from both of its huge arms.

flavor.27: This Ultra Beast came from the Ultra Wormhole. It seems not to attack enemies on its own, but its sharp body is a dangerous weapon in itself.
flavor.28: One of the Ultra Beast life-forms, it was observed cutting down a gigantic steel tower with one stroke of its blade.
flavor.29: This Ultra Beast’s body, which is as thin as paper, is like a sharpened sword.
flavor.30: Although it’s alien to this world and a danger here, it’s apparently a common organism in the world where it normally lives.
flavor.latest: This Ultra Beast’s body, which is as thin as paper, is like a sharpened sword.

flavor.27: It has gobbled mountains and swallowed whole buildings, according to reports. It’s one of the Ultra Beasts.
flavor.28: A dangerous Ultra Beast, it appears to be eating constantly, but for some reason its droppings have never been found.
flavor.29: Although it’s alien to this world and a danger here, it’s apparently a common organism in the world where it normally lives.
flavor.30: An unknown life-form called a UB. It may be constantly hungry—it is certainly always devouring something.
flavor.latest: Although it’s alien to this world and a danger here, it’s apparently a common organism in the world where it normally lives.

flavor.27: Reminiscent of the Ultra Beasts, this life-form, apparently asleep underground, is thought to have come from another world in ancient times.
flavor.28: Light is apparently the source of its energy. It has an extraordinarily vicious disposition and is constantly firing off laser beams.
flavor.29: It looks somehow pained as it rages around in search of light, which serves as its energy. It’s apparently from another world.
flavor.30: Light is the source of its energy. If it isn’t devouring light, impurities build up in it and on it, and Necrozma darkens and stops moving.
flavor.33: It survives by absorbing light. After a long time spent slumbering underground, impurities accumulated within it, causing its body to darken.
flavor.34: It needs light to survive, and it goes on a rampage seeking it out. Its laser beams will cut anything to pieces.
flavor.latest: It survives by absorbing light. After a long time spent slumbering underground, impurities accumulated within it, causing its body to darken.

flavor.27: This artificial Pokémon, constructed more than 500 years ago, can understand human speech but cannot itself speak.
flavor.28: Its mechanized body is merely a vessel. Its true self is its Soul-Heart, an artificial soul.
flavor.29: It synchronizes its consciousness with others to understand their feelings. This faculty makes it useful for taking care of people.
flavor.30: Built roughly 500 years ago by a scientist, the part called the Soul-Heart is the actual life-form.
flavor.latest: It synchronizes its consciousness with others to understand their feelings. This faculty makes it useful for taking care of people.

flavor.27: Able to conceal itself in shadows, it never appears before humans, so its very existence was the stuff of myth.
flavor.28: It lurks in the shadows of others, copying their movements and powers. This Pokémon is craven and cowering.
flavor.29: It slips into the shadows of others and mimics their powers and movements. As it improves, it becomes stronger than those it’s imitating.
flavor.30: It sinks into the shadows of people and Pokémon, where it can understand their feelings and copy their capabilities.
flavor.33: By slipping into the shadow of a martial arts master and copying their movements, this Pokémon learned the ultimate techniques.
flavor.34: This Pokémon can conceal itself in any shadow, so it went undiscovered for a long time.
flavor.latest: By slipping into the shadow of a martial arts master and copying their movements, this Pokémon learned the ultimate techniques.

flavor.29: This Ultra Beast is well enough liked to be chosen as a first partner in its own world.
flavor.30: An Ultra Beast that lives in a different world, it cackles wildly as it sprays its opponents with poison from the needles on its head.
flavor.latest: This Ultra Beast is well enough liked to be chosen as a first partner in its own world.

flavor.29: It stores hundreds of liters of poisonous liquid inside its body. It is one of the organisms known as UBs.
flavor.30: One kind of Ultra Beast, it fires a glowing, venomous liquid from its needles. This liquid is also immensely adhesive.
flavor.latest: It stores hundreds of liters of poisonous liquid inside its body. It is one of the organisms known as UBs.

flavor.29: It appeared from an Ultra Wormhole. Each one appears to be made up of many life-forms stacked one on top of each other.
flavor.30: When stone walls started moving and attacking, the brute’s true identity was this mysterious life-form, which brings to mind an Ultra Beast.
flavor.latest: It appeared from an Ultra Wormhole. Each one appears to be made up of many life-forms stacked one on top of each other.

flavor.29: It slithers toward people. Then, without warning, it triggers the explosion of its own head. It’s apparently one kind of Ultra Beast.
flavor.30: A UB that appeared from an Ultra Wormhole, it causes explosions, then takes advantage of opponents’ surprise to rob them of their vitality.
flavor.latest: It slithers toward people. Then, without warning, it triggers the explosion of its own head. It’s apparently one kind of Ultra Beast.

flavor.29: It electrifies its claws and tears its opponents apart with them. Even if they dodge its attack, they’ll be electrocuted by the flying sparks.
flavor.30: It approaches its enemies at the speed of lightning, then tears them limb from limb with its sharp claws.
flavor.33: It runs as fast as lightning strikes, shredding its opponents with its high-voltage claws.
flavor.34: Electricity sparks from the pads on its limbs. Wherever Zeraora runs, lightning flashes and thunder echoes.
flavor.latest: It runs as fast as lightning strikes, shredding its opponents with its high-voltage claws.

flavor.31: It melts particles of iron and other metals found in the subsoil, so it can absorb them into its body of molten steel.
flavor.32: It melts particles of iron and other metals found in the subsoil, so it can absorb them into its body of molten steel.
flavor.33: It dissolves and eats metal. Circulating liquid metal within its body is how it generates energy.
flavor.34: They live as a group, but when the time comes, one strong Meltan will absorb all the others and evolve.
flavor.latest: It dissolves and eats metal. Circulating liquid metal within its body is how it generates energy.

flavor.31: Revered long ago for its capacity to create iron from nothing, for some reason it has come back to life after 3,000 years.
flavor.32: Revered long ago for its capacity to create iron from nothing, for some reason it has come back to life after 3,000 years.
flavor.33: At the end of its life-span, Melmetal will rust and fall apart. The small shards left behind will eventually be reborn as Meltan.
flavor.34: Centrifugal force is behind the punches of Melmetal’s heavy hex-nut arms. Melmetal is said to deliver the strongest punches of all Pokémon.
flavor.latest: At the end of its life-span, Melmetal will rust and fall apart. The small shards left behind will eventually be reborn as Meltan.

flavor.33: When it uses its special stick to strike up a beat, the sound waves produced carry revitalizing energy to the plants and flowers in the area.
flavor.34: It attacks with rapid beats of its stick. As it strikes with amazing speed, it gets more and more pumped.
flavor.latest: When it uses its special stick to strike up a beat, the sound waves produced carry revitalizing energy to the plants and flowers in the area.

flavor.33: The faster a Thwackey can beat out a rhythm with its two sticks, the more respect it wins from its peers.
flavor.34: When it’s drumming out rapid beats in battle, it gets so caught up in the rhythm that it won’t even notice that it’s already knocked out its opponent.
flavor.latest: The faster a Thwackey can beat out a rhythm with its two sticks, the more respect it wins from its peers.

flavor.33: By drumming, it taps into the power of its special tree stump. The roots of the stump follow its direction in battle.
flavor.34: The one with the best drumming techniques becomes the boss of the troop. It has a gentle disposition and values harmony among its group.
flavor.latest: By drumming, it taps into the power of its special tree stump. The roots of the stump follow its direction in battle.

flavor.33: A warm-up of running around gets fire energy coursing through this Pokémon’s body. Once that happens, it’s ready to fight at full power.
flavor.34: It has special pads on the backs of its feet, and one on its nose. Once it’s raring to fight, these pads radiate tremendous heat.
flavor.latest: A warm-up of running around gets fire energy coursing through this Pokémon’s body. Once that happens, it’s ready to fight at full power.

flavor.33: Its thick and fluffy fur protects it from the cold and enables it to use hotter fire moves.
flavor.34: It kicks berries right off the branches of trees and then juggles them with its feet, practicing its footwork.
flavor.latest: Its thick and fluffy fur protects it from the cold and enables it to use hotter fire moves.

flavor.33: It juggles a pebble with its feet, turning it into a burning soccer ball. Its shots strike opponents hard and leave them scorched.
flavor.34: It’s skilled at both offense and defense, and it gets pumped up when cheered on. But if it starts showboating, it could put itself in a tough spot.
flavor.latest: It juggles a pebble with its feet, turning it into a burning soccer ball. Its shots strike opponents hard and leave them scorched.

flavor.33: When scared, this Pokémon cries. Its tears pack the chemical punch of 100 onions, and attackers won’t be able to resist weeping.
flavor.34: When it gets wet, its skin changes color, and this Pokémon becomes invisible as if it were camouflaged.
flavor.latest: When scared, this Pokémon cries. Its tears pack the chemical punch of 100 onions, and attackers won’t be able to resist weeping.

flavor.33: A clever combatant, this Pokémon battles using water balloons created with moisture secreted from its palms.
flavor.34: Highly intelligent but also very lazy, it keeps enemies out of its territory by laying traps everywhere.
flavor.latest: A clever combatant, this Pokémon battles using water balloons created with moisture secreted from its palms.

flavor.33: It has many hidden capabilities, such as fingertips that can shoot water and a membrane on its back that it can use to glide through the air.
flavor.34: Its nictitating membranes let it pick out foes’ weak points so it can precisely blast them with water that shoots from its fingertips at Mach 3.
flavor.latest: It has many hidden capabilities, such as fingertips that can shoot water and a membrane on its back that it can use to glide through the air.

flavor.33: Found throughout the Galar region, this Pokémon becomes uneasy if its cheeks are ever completely empty of berries.
flavor.34: It eats berries nonstop—a habit that has made it more resilient than it looks. It’ll show up on farms, searching for yet more berries.
flavor.latest: Found throughout the Galar region, this Pokémon becomes uneasy if its cheeks are ever completely empty of berries.

flavor.33: It stashes berries in its tail—so many berries that they fall out constantly. But this Pokémon is a bit slow-witted, so it doesn’t notice the loss.
flavor.34: Common throughout the Galar region, this Pokémon has strong teeth and can chew through the toughest of berry shells.
flavor.latest: It stashes berries in its tail—so many berries that they fall out constantly. But this Pokémon is a bit slow-witted, so it doesn’t notice the loss.

flavor.33: It will bravely challenge any opponent, no matter how powerful. This Pokémon benefits from every battle—even a defeat increases its strength a bit.
flavor.34: Jumping nimbly about, this small-bodied Pokémon takes advantage of even the slightest opportunity to disorient larger opponents.
flavor.latest: It will bravely challenge any opponent, no matter how powerful. This Pokémon benefits from every battle—even a defeat increases its strength a bit.

flavor.33: Smart enough to use tools in battle, these Pokémon have been seen picking up rocks and flinging them or using ropes to wrap up enemies.
flavor.34: The lessons of many harsh battles have taught it how to accurately judge an opponent’s strength.
flavor.latest: Smart enough to use tools in battle, these Pokémon have been seen picking up rocks and flinging them or using ropes to wrap up enemies.

flavor.33: This Pokémon reigns supreme in the skies of the Galar region. The black luster of its steel body could drive terror into the heart of any foe.
flavor.34: With their great intellect and flying skills, these Pokémon very successfully act as the Galar region’s airborne taxi service.
flavor.latest: This Pokémon reigns supreme in the skies of the Galar region. The black luster of its steel body could drive terror into the heart of any foe.

flavor.33: A constant collector of information, this Pokémon is very smart. Very strong is what it isn’t.
flavor.34: Often found in gardens, this Pokémon has hairs on its body that it uses to assess its surroundings.
flavor.latest: A constant collector of information, this Pokémon is very smart. Very strong is what it isn’t.

flavor.33: It barely moves, but it’s still alive. Hiding in its shell without food or water seems to have awakened its psychic powers.
flavor.34: As it grows inside its shell, it uses its psychic abilities to monitor the outside world and prepare for evolution.
flavor.latest: It barely moves, but it’s still alive. Hiding in its shell without food or water seems to have awakened its psychic powers.

flavor.33: It’s famous for its high level of intelligence, and the large size of its brain is proof that it also possesses immense psychic power.
flavor.34: It emits psychic energy to observe and study what’s around it—and what’s around it can include things over six miles away.
flavor.latest: It’s famous for its high level of intelligence, and the large size of its brain is proof that it also possesses immense psychic power.

flavor.33: Aided by the soft pads on its feet, it silently raids the food stores of other Pokémon. It survives off its ill-gotten gains.
flavor.34: Cunning and cautious, this Pokémon survives by stealing food from others. It erases its tracks with swipes of its tail as it makes off with its plunder.
flavor.latest: Aided by the soft pads on its feet, it silently raids the food stores of other Pokémon. It survives off its ill-gotten gains.

flavor.33: It secretly marks potential targets with a scent. By following the scent, it stalks its targets and steals from them when they least expect it.
flavor.34: With a lithe body and sharp claws, it goes around stealing food and eggs. Boltund is its natural enemy.
flavor.latest: It secretly marks potential targets with a scent. By following the scent, it stalks its targets and steals from them when they least expect it.

flavor.33: It anchors itself in the ground with its single leg, then basks in the sun. After absorbing enough sunlight, its petals spread as it blooms brilliantly.
flavor.34: It whirls around in the wind while singing a joyous song. This delightful display has charmed many into raising this Pokémon.
flavor.latest: It anchors itself in the ground with its single leg, then basks in the sun. After absorbing enough sunlight, its petals spread as it blooms brilliantly.

flavor.33: The seeds attached to its cotton fluff are full of nutrients. It spreads them on the wind so that plants and other Pokémon can benefit from them.
flavor.34: The cotton on the head of this Pokémon can be spun into a glossy, gorgeous yarn—a Galar regional specialty.
flavor.latest: The seeds attached to its cotton fluff are full of nutrients. It spreads them on the wind so that plants and other Pokémon can benefit from them.

flavor.33: Its curly fleece is such an effective cushion that this Pokémon could fall off a cliff and stand right back up at the bottom, unharmed.
flavor.34: If its fleece grows too long, Wooloo won’t be able to move. Cloth made with the wool of this Pokémon is surprisingly strong.
flavor.latest: Its curly fleece is such an effective cushion that this Pokémon could fall off a cliff and stand right back up at the bottom, unharmed.

flavor.33: Weave a carpet from its springy wool, and you end up with something closer to a trampoline. You’ll start to bounce the moment you set foot on it.
flavor.34: Its majestic horns are meant only to impress the opposite gender. They never see use in battle.
flavor.latest: Weave a carpet from its springy wool, and you end up with something closer to a trampoline. You’ll start to bounce the moment you set foot on it.

flavor.33: Apparently the itch of its teething impels it to snap its jaws at anything in front of it.
flavor.34: It starts off battles by attacking with its rock-hard horn, but as soon as the opponent flinches, this Pokémon bites down and never lets go.
flavor.latest: Apparently the itch of its teething impels it to snap its jaws at anything in front of it.

flavor.33: With jaws that can shear through steel rods, this highly aggressive Pokémon chomps down on its unfortunate prey.
flavor.34: This Pokémon rapidly extends its retractable neck to sink its sharp fangs into distant enemies and take them down.
flavor.latest: With jaws that can shear through steel rods, this highly aggressive Pokémon chomps down on its unfortunate prey.

flavor.33: This Pokémon is very popular as a herding dog in the Galar region. As it runs, it generates electricity from the base of its tail.
flavor.34: This gluttonous Pokémon only assists people with their work because it wants treats. As it runs, it crackles with electricity.
flavor.latest: This Pokémon is very popular as a herding dog in the Galar region. As it runs, it generates electricity from the base of its tail.

flavor.33: This Pokémon generates electricity and channels it into its legs to keep them going strong. Boltund can run nonstop for three full days.
flavor.34: It sends electricity through its legs to boost their strength. Running at top speed, it easily breaks 50 mph.
flavor.latest: This Pokémon generates electricity and channels it into its legs to keep them going strong. Boltund can run nonstop for three full days.

flavor.33: Most of its body has the same composition as coal. Fittingly, this Pokémon was first discovered in coal mines about 400 years ago.
flavor.34: It can race around like a unicycle, even on rough, rocky terrain. Burning coal sustains it.
flavor.latest: Most of its body has the same composition as coal. Fittingly, this Pokémon was first discovered in coal mines about 400 years ago.

flavor.33: It forms coal inside its body. Coal dropped by this Pokémon once helped fuel the lives of people in the Galar region.
flavor.34: By rapidly rolling its legs, it can travel at over 18 mph. The temperature of the flames it breathes exceeds 1,800 degrees Fahrenheit.
flavor.latest: It forms coal inside its body. Coal dropped by this Pokémon once helped fuel the lives of people in the Galar region.

flavor.33: It’s usually peaceful, but the vandalism of mines enrages it. Offenders will be incinerated with flames that reach 2,700 degrees Fahrenheit.
flavor.34: While it’s engaged in battle, its mountain of coal will burn bright red, sending off sparks that scorch the surrounding area.
flavor.latest: It’s usually peaceful, but the vandalism of mines enrages it. Offenders will be incinerated with flames that reach 2,700 degrees Fahrenheit.

flavor.33: It spends its entire life inside an apple. It hides from its natural enemies, bird Pokémon, by pretending it’s just an apple and nothing more.
flavor.34: As soon as it’s born, it burrows into an apple. Not only does the apple serve as its food source, but the flavor of the fruit determines its evolution.
flavor.latest: It spends its entire life inside an apple. It hides from its natural enemies, bird Pokémon, by pretending it’s just an apple and nothing more.

flavor.33: It ate a sour apple, and that induced its evolution. In its cheeks, it stores an acid capable of causing chemical burns.
flavor.34: It flies on wings of apple skin and spits a powerful acid. It can also change its shape into that of an apple.
flavor.latest: It ate a sour apple, and that induced its evolution. In its cheeks, it stores an acid capable of causing chemical burns.

flavor.33: Eating a sweet apple caused its evolution. A nectarous scent wafts from its body, luring in the bug Pokémon it preys on.
flavor.34: Its body is covered in sweet nectar, and the skin on its back is especially yummy. Children used to have it as a snack.
flavor.latest: Eating a sweet apple caused its evolution. A nectarous scent wafts from its body, luring in the bug Pokémon it preys on.

flavor.33: As it digs, it swallows sand and stores it in its neck pouch. The pouch can hold more than 17 pounds of sand.
flavor.34: It spews sand from its nostrils. While the enemy is blinded, it burrows into the ground to hide.
flavor.latest: As it digs, it swallows sand and stores it in its neck pouch. The pouch can hold more than 17 pounds of sand.

flavor.33: When it contracts its body, over 220 pounds of sand sprays from its nose. If it ever runs out of sand, it becomes disheartened.
flavor.34: Its unique style of coiling allows it to blast sand out of its sand sac more efficiently.
flavor.latest: When it contracts its body, over 220 pounds of sand sprays from its nose. If it ever runs out of sand, it becomes disheartened.

flavor.33: It’s so strong that it can knock out some opponents in a single hit, but it also may forget what it’s battling midfight.
flavor.34: This hungry Pokémon swallows Arrokuda whole. Occasionally, it makes a mistake and tries to swallow a Pokémon other than its preferred prey.
flavor.latest: It’s so strong that it can knock out some opponents in a single hit, but it also may forget what it’s battling midfight.

flavor.33: If it sees any movement around it, this Pokémon charges for it straightaway, leading with its sharply pointed jaw. It’s very proud of that jaw.
flavor.34: After it’s eaten its fill, its movements become extremely sluggish. That’s when Cramorant swallows it up.
flavor.latest: If it sees any movement around it, this Pokémon charges for it straightaway, leading with its sharply pointed jaw. It’s very proud of that jaw.

flavor.33: This Pokémon has a jaw that’s as sharp as a spear and as strong as steel. Apparently Barraskewda’s flesh is surprisingly tasty, too.
flavor.34: It spins its tail fins to propel itself, surging forward at speeds of over 100 knots before ramming prey and spearing into them.
flavor.latest: This Pokémon has a jaw that’s as sharp as a spear and as strong as steel. Apparently Barraskewda’s flesh is surprisingly tasty, too.

flavor.33: It stores poison in an internal poison sac and secretes that poison through its skin. If you touch this Pokémon, a tingling sensation follows.
flavor.34: It manipulates the chemical makeup of its poison to produce electricity. The voltage is weak, but it can cause a tingling paralysis.
flavor.latest: It stores poison in an internal poison sac and secretes that poison through its skin. If you touch this Pokémon, a tingling sensation follows.

flavor.33: When this Pokémon sounds as if it’s strumming a guitar, it’s actually clawing at the protrusions on its chest to generate electricity.
