flavor.34: This short-tempered and aggressive Pokémon chugs stagnant water to absorb any toxins it might contain.
flavor.latest: When this Pokémon sounds as if it’s strumming a guitar, it’s actually clawing at the protrusions on its chest to generate electricity.

flavor.33: It stores flammable gas in its body and uses it to generate heat. The yellow sections on its belly get particularly hot.
flavor.34: It wraps prey up with its heated body, cooking them in its coils. Once they’re well-done, it will voraciously nibble them down to the last morsel.
flavor.latest: It stores flammable gas in its body and uses it to generate heat. The yellow sections on its belly get particularly hot.

flavor.33: When it heats up, its body temperature reaches about 1,500 degrees Fahrenheit. It lashes its body like a whip and launches itself at enemies.
flavor.34: While its burning body is already dangerous on its own, this excessively hostile Pokémon also has large and very sharp fangs.
flavor.latest: When it heats up, its body temperature reaches about 1,500 degrees Fahrenheit. It lashes its body like a whip and launches itself at enemies.

flavor.33: It’s very curious, but its means of investigating things is to try to punch them with its tentacles. The search for food is what brings it onto land.
flavor.34: Its tentacles tear off easily, but it isn’t alarmed when that happens—it knows they’ll grow back. It’s about as smart as a three-year-old.
flavor.latest: It’s very curious, but its means of investigating things is to try to punch them with its tentacles. The search for food is what brings it onto land.

flavor.33: A body made up of nothing but muscle makes the grappling moves this Pokémon performs with its tentacles tremendously powerful.
flavor.34: Searching for an opponent to test its skills against, it emerges onto land. Once the battle is over, it returns to the sea.
flavor.latest: A body made up of nothing but muscle makes the grappling moves this Pokémon performs with its tentacles tremendously powerful.

flavor.33: This Pokémon is said to have been born when a lonely spirit possessed a cold, leftover cup of tea.
flavor.34: The teacup in which this Pokémon makes its home is a famous piece of antique tableware. Many forgeries are in circulation.
flavor.latest: This Pokémon is said to have been born when a lonely spirit possessed a cold, leftover cup of tea.

flavor.33: This species lives in antique teapots. Most pots are forgeries, but on rare occasions, an authentic work is found.
flavor.34: Leaving leftover black tea unattended is asking for this Pokémon to come along and pour itself into it, turning the tea into a new Polteageist.
flavor.latest: This species lives in antique teapots. Most pots are forgeries, but on rare occasions, an authentic work is found.

flavor.33: Via the protrusion on its head, it senses other creatures’ emotions. If you don’t have a calm disposition, it will never warm up to you.
flavor.34: If this Pokémon senses a strong emotion, it will run away as fast as it can. It prefers areas without people.
flavor.latest: Via the protrusion on its head, it senses other creatures’ emotions. If you don’t have a calm disposition, it will never warm up to you.

flavor.33: No matter who you are, if you bring strong emotions near this Pokémon, it will silence you violently.
flavor.34: Using the braids on its head, it pummels foes to get them to quiet down. One blow from those braids would knock out a professional boxer.
flavor.latest: No matter who you are, if you bring strong emotions near this Pokémon, it will silence you violently.

flavor.33: It emits psychic power strong enough to cause headaches as a deterrent to the approach of others.
flavor.34: If you’re too loud around it, you risk being torn apart by the claws on its tentacle. This Pokémon is also known as the Forest Witch.
flavor.latest: It emits psychic power strong enough to cause headaches as a deterrent to the approach of others.

flavor.33: Through its nose, it sucks in the emanations produced by people and Pokémon when they feel annoyed. It thrives off this negative energy.
flavor.34: It sneaks into people’s homes, stealing things and feasting on the negative energy of the frustrated occupants.
flavor.latest: Through its nose, it sucks in the emanations produced by people and Pokémon when they feel annoyed. It thrives off this negative energy.

flavor.33: When it gets down on all fours as if to beg for forgiveness, it’s trying to lure opponents in so that it can stab them with its spear-like hair.
flavor.34: With sly cunning, it tries to lure people into the woods. Some believe it to have the power to make crops grow.
flavor.latest: When it gets down on all fours as if to beg for forgiveness, it’s trying to lure opponents in so that it can stab them with its spear-like hair.

flavor.33: With the hair wrapped around its body helping to enhance its muscles, this Pokémon can overwhelm even Machamp.
flavor.34: Its hairs work like muscle fibers. When its hairs unfurl, they latch on to opponents, ensnaring them as tentacles would.
flavor.latest: With the hair wrapped around its body helping to enhance its muscles, this Pokémon can overwhelm even Machamp.

flavor.33: Its voice is staggering in volume. Obstagoon has a tendency to take on a threatening posture and shout—this move is known as Obstruct.
flavor.34: It evolved after experiencing numerous fights. While crossing its arms, it lets out a shout that would make any opponent flinch.
flavor.latest: Its voice is staggering in volume. Obstagoon has a tendency to take on a threatening posture and shout—this move is known as Obstruct.

flavor.33: What appears to be an iron helmet is actually hardened hair. This Pokémon lives for the thrill of battle.
flavor.34: After many battles, it evolved dangerous claws that come together to form daggers when extended.
flavor.latest: What appears to be an iron helmet is actually hardened hair. This Pokémon lives for the thrill of battle.

flavor.33: Its shell is overflowing with its heightened otherworldly energy. The ectoplasm serves as protection for this Pokémon’s core spirit.
flavor.34: Be cautious of the ectoplasmic body surrounding its soul. You’ll become stiff as stone if you touch it.
flavor.latest: Its shell is overflowing with its heightened otherworldly energy. The ectoplasm serves as protection for this Pokémon’s core spirit.

flavor.33: Only Farfetch’d that have survived many battles can attain this evolution. When this Pokémon’s leek withers, it will retire from combat.
flavor.34: After deflecting attacks with its hard leaf shield, it strikes back with its sharp leek stalk. The leek stalk is both weapon and food.
flavor.latest: Only Farfetch’d that have survived many battles can attain this evolution. When this Pokémon’s leek withers, it will retire from combat.

flavor.33: It’s highly skilled at tap-dancing. It waves its cane of ice in time with its graceful movements.
flavor.34: Its amusing movements make it very popular. It releases its psychic power from the pattern on its belly.
flavor.latest: It’s highly skilled at tap-dancing. It waves its cane of ice in time with its graceful movements.

flavor.33: A powerful curse was woven into an ancient painting. After absorbing the spirit of a Yamask, the painting began to move.
flavor.34: Never touch its shadowlike body, or you’ll be shown the horrific memories behind the picture carved into it.
flavor.latest: A powerful curse was woven into an ancient painting. After absorbing the spirit of a Yamask, the painting began to move.

flavor.33: This Pokémon was born from sweet-smelling particles in the air. Its body is made of cream.
flavor.34: They say that any patisserie visited by Milcery is guaranteed success and good fortune.
flavor.latest: This Pokémon was born from sweet-smelling particles in the air. Its body is made of cream.

flavor.33: When it trusts a Trainer, it will treat them to berries it’s decorated with cream.
flavor.34: When Alcremie is content, the cream it secretes from its hands becomes sweeter and richer.
flavor.latest: When it trusts a Trainer, it will treat them to berries it’s decorated with cream.

flavor.33: Five of them are troopers, and one is the brass. The brass’s orders are absolute.
flavor.34: The six of them work together as one Pokémon. Teamwork is also their battle strategy, and they constantly change their formation as they fight.
flavor.latest: Five of them are troopers, and one is the brass. The brass’s orders are absolute.

flavor.33: It feeds on seaweed, using its teeth to scrape it off rocks. Electric current flows from the tips of its spines.
flavor.34: It stores electricity in each spine. Even if one gets broken off, it still continues to emit electricity for at least three hours.
flavor.latest: It feeds on seaweed, using its teeth to scrape it off rocks. Electric current flows from the tips of its spines.

flavor.33: It spits out thread imbued with a frigid sort of energy and uses it to tie its body to branches, disguising itself as an icicle while it sleeps.
flavor.34: It eats snow that piles up on the ground. The more snow it eats, the bigger and more impressive the spikes on its back grow.
flavor.latest: It spits out thread imbued with a frigid sort of energy and uses it to tie its body to branches, disguising itself as an icicle while it sleeps.

flavor.33: Icy scales fall from its wings like snow as it flies over fields and mountains. The temperature of its wings is less than −290 degrees Fahrenheit.
flavor.34: It shows no mercy to any who desecrate fields and mountains. It will fly around on its icy wings, causing a blizzard to chase offenders away.
flavor.latest: Icy scales fall from its wings like snow as it flies over fields and mountains. The temperature of its wings is less than −290 degrees Fahrenheit.

flavor.33: It stands in grasslands, watching the sun’s descent from zenith to horizon. This Pokémon has a talent for delivering dynamic kicks.
flavor.34: Once a year, on a specific date and at a specific time, they gather out of nowhere and form up in a circle.
flavor.latest: It stands in grasslands, watching the sun’s descent from zenith to horizon. This Pokémon has a talent for delivering dynamic kicks.

flavor.33: It drifted in on the flow of ocean waters from a frigid place. It keeps its head iced constantly to make sure it stays nice and cold.
flavor.34: This Pokémon keeps its heat-sensitive head cool with ice. It fishes for its food, dangling its single hair into the sea to lure in prey.
flavor.latest: It drifted in on the flow of ocean waters from a frigid place. It keeps its head iced constantly to make sure it stays nice and cold.

flavor.33: It uses the horns on its head to sense the emotions of others. Males will act as valets for those they serve, looking after their every need.
flavor.34: Through its horns, it can pick up on the emotions of creatures around it. Positive emotions are the source of its strength.
flavor.latest: It uses the horns on its head to sense the emotions of others. Males will act as valets for those they serve, looking after their every need.

flavor.33: As it eats the seeds stored up in its pocket-like pouches, this Pokémon is not just satisfying its constant hunger. It’s also generating electricity.
flavor.34: It carries electrically roasted seeds with it as if they’re precious treasures. No matter how much it eats, it always gets hungry again in short order.
flavor.latest: As it eats the seeds stored up in its pocket-like pouches, this Pokémon is not just satisfying its constant hunger. It’s also generating electricity.

flavor.33: It digs up the ground with its trunk. It’s also very strong, being able to carry loads of over five tons without any problem at all.
flavor.34: If a job requires serious strength, this Pokémon will excel at it. Its copper body tarnishes in the rain, turning a vibrant green color.
flavor.latest: It digs up the ground with its trunk. It’s also very strong, being able to carry loads of over five tons without any problem at all.

flavor.33: They came over from another region long ago and worked together with humans. Their green skin is resistant to water.
flavor.34: These Pokémon live in herds. Their trunks have incredible grip strength, strong enough to crush giant rocks into powder.
flavor.latest: They came over from another region long ago and worked together with humans. Their green skin is resistant to water.

flavor.33: In ancient times, it was unbeatable thanks to its powerful lower body, but it went extinct anyway after it depleted all its plant-based food sources.
flavor.34: The powerful muscles in its tail generate its electricity. Compared to its lower body, its upper half is entirely too small.
flavor.latest: In ancient times, it was unbeatable thanks to its powerful lower body, but it went extinct anyway after it depleted all its plant-based food sources.

flavor.33: The shaking of its freezing upper half is what generates its electricity. It has a hard time walking around.
flavor.34: This Pokémon lived on prehistoric seashores and was able to preserve food with the ice on its body. It went extinct because it moved so slowly.
flavor.latest: The shaking of its freezing upper half is what generates its electricity. It has a hard time walking around.

flavor.33: Powerful legs and jaws made it the apex predator of its time. Its own overhunting of its prey was what drove it to extinction.
flavor.34: Its mighty legs are capable of running at speeds exceeding 40 mph, but this Pokémon can’t breathe unless it’s underwater.
flavor.latest: Powerful legs and jaws made it the apex predator of its time. Its own overhunting of its prey was what drove it to extinction.

flavor.33: Though it’s able to capture prey by freezing its surroundings, it has trouble eating the prey afterward because its mouth is on top of its head.
flavor.34: The skin on its face is impervious to attack, but breathing difficulties made this Pokémon go extinct anyway.
flavor.latest: Though it’s able to capture prey by freezing its surroundings, it has trouble eating the prey afterward because its mouth is on top of its head.

flavor.33: Its body resembles polished metal, and it’s both lightweight and strong. The only drawback is that it rusts easily.
flavor.34: The special metal that composes its body is very light, so this Pokémon has considerable agility. It lives in caves because it dislikes the rain.
flavor.latest: Its body resembles polished metal, and it’s both lightweight and strong. The only drawback is that it rusts easily.

flavor.33: After being reborn as a ghost Pokémon, Dreepy wanders the areas it used to inhabit back when it was alive in prehistoric seas.
flavor.34: If this weak Pokémon is by itself, a mere child could defeat it. But if Dreepy has friends to help it train, it can evolve and become much stronger.
flavor.latest: After being reborn as a ghost Pokémon, Dreepy wanders the areas it used to inhabit back when it was alive in prehistoric seas.

flavor.33: It’s capable of flying faster than 120 mph. It battles alongside Dreepy and dotes on them until they successfully evolve.
flavor.34: Without a Dreepy to place on its head and care for, it gets so uneasy it’ll try to substitute any Pokémon it finds for the missing Dreepy.
flavor.latest: It’s capable of flying faster than 120 mph. It battles alongside Dreepy and dotes on them until they successfully evolve.

flavor.33: When it isn’t battling, it keeps Dreepy in the holes on its horns. Once a fight starts, it launches the Dreepy like supersonic missiles.

flavor.latest: When it isn’t battling, it keeps Dreepy in the holes on its horns. Once a fight starts, it launches the Dreepy like supersonic missiles.

flavor.33: Known as a legendary hero, this Pokémon absorbs metal particles, transforming them into a weapon it uses to battle.
flavor.34: This Pokémon has slumbered for many years. Some say it’s Zamazenta’s elder sister—others say the two Pokémon are rivals.
flavor.latest: Known as a legendary hero, this Pokémon absorbs metal particles, transforming them into a weapon it uses to battle.

flavor.33: In times past, it worked together with a king of the people to save the Galar region. It absorbs metal that it then uses in battle.
flavor.34: This Pokémon slept for aeons while in the form of a statue. It was asleep for so long, people forgot that it ever existed.
flavor.latest: In times past, it worked together with a king of the people to save the Galar region. It absorbs metal that it then uses in battle.

flavor.33: The core on its chest absorbs energy emanating from the lands of the Galar region. This energy is what allows Eternatus to stay active.
flavor.34: It was inside a meteorite that fell 20,000 years ago. There seems to be a connection between this Pokémon and the Dynamax phenomenon.
flavor.latest: The core on its chest absorbs energy emanating from the lands of the Galar region. This energy is what allows Eternatus to stay active.

flavor.33: Kubfu trains hard to perfect its moves. The moves it masters will determine which form it takes when it evolves.
flavor.34: If Kubfu pulls the long white hair on its head, its fighting spirit heightens and power wells up from the depths of its belly.
flavor.latest: Kubfu trains hard to perfect its moves. The moves it masters will determine which form it takes when it evolves.

flavor.33: This form of Urshifu is a strong believer in the one-hit KO. Its strategy is to leap in close to foes and land a devastating blow with a hardened fist.
flavor.34: Inhabiting the mountains of a distant region, this Pokémon races across sheer cliffs, training its legs and refining its moves.
flavor.latest: This form of Urshifu is a strong believer in the one-hit KO. Its strategy is to leap in close to foes and land a devastating blow with a hardened fist.

flavor.33: Within dense forests, this Pokémon lives in a pack with others of its kind. It’s incredibly aggressive, and the other Pokémon of the forest fear it.
flavor.34: Once the vines on Zarude’s body tear off, they become nutrients in the soil. This helps the plants of the forest grow.
flavor.latest: Within dense forests, this Pokémon lives in a pack with others of its kind. It’s incredibly aggressive, and the other Pokémon of the forest fear it.

flavor.33: This Pokémon is a cluster of electrical energy. It’s said that removing the rings on Regieleki’s body will unleash the Pokémon’s latent power.
flavor.34: Its entire body is made up of a single organ that generates electrical energy. Regieleki is capable of creating all Galar’s electricity.
flavor.latest: This Pokémon is a cluster of electrical energy. It’s said that removing the rings on Regieleki’s body will unleash the Pokémon’s latent power.

flavor.33: An academic theory proposes that Regidrago’s arms were once the head of an ancient dragon Pokémon. The theory remains unproven.
flavor.34: Its body is composed of crystallized dragon energy. Regidrago is said to have the powers of every dragon Pokémon.
flavor.latest: An academic theory proposes that Regidrago’s arms were once the head of an ancient dragon Pokémon. The theory remains unproven.

flavor.33: Glastrier emits intense cold from its hooves. It’s also a belligerent Pokémon—anything it wants, it takes by force.
flavor.34: Glastrier has tremendous physical strength, and the mask of ice covering its face is 100 times harder than diamond.
flavor.latest: Glastrier emits intense cold from its hooves. It’s also a belligerent Pokémon—anything it wants, it takes by force.

flavor.33: It probes its surroundings with all its senses save one—it doesn’t use its sense of sight. Spectrier’s kicks are said to separate soul from body.
flavor.34: As it dashes through the night, Spectrier absorbs the life-force of sleeping creatures. It craves silence and solitude.
flavor.latest: It probes its surroundings with all its senses save one—it doesn’t use its sense of sight. Spectrier’s kicks are said to separate soul from body.

flavor.33: Calyrex is a merciful Pokémon, capable of providing healing and blessings. It reigned over the Galar region in times of yore.
flavor.34: Calyrex is known in legend as a king that ruled over Galar in ancient times. It has the power to cause hearts to mend and plants to spring forth.
flavor.latest: Calyrex is a merciful Pokémon, capable of providing healing and blessings. It reigned over the Galar region in times of yore.

flavor.39: The black orbs shine with an uncanny light when the Pokémon is erecting invisible barriers. The fur shed from its beard retains heat well and is a highly useful material for winter clothing.
flavor.latest: The black orbs shine with an uncanny light when the Pokémon is erecting invisible barriers. The fur shed from its beard retains heat well and is a highly useful material for winter clothing.

flavor.39: A violent creature that fells towering trees with its crude axes and shields itself with hard stone. If one should chance upon this Pokémon in the wilds, one's only recourse is to flee.
flavor.latest: A violent creature that fells towering trees with its crude axes and shields itself with hard stone. If one should chance upon this Pokémon in the wilds, one's only recourse is to flee.

flavor.39: I believe it was Hisui's swampy terrain that gave Ursaluna its burly physique and newfound capacity to manipulate peat at will.
flavor.latest: I believe it was Hisui's swampy terrain that gave Ursaluna its burly physique and newfound capacity to manipulate peat at will.

flavor.39: Clads itself in the souls of comrades that perished before fulfilling their goals of journeying upstream. No other species throughout all Hisui's rivers is Basculegion's equal.
flavor.latest: Clads itself in the souls of comrades that perished before fulfilling their goals of journeying upstream. No other species throughout all Hisui's rivers is Basculegion's equal.

flavor.39: Because of Sneasler's virulent poison and daunting physical prowess, no other species could hope to best it on the frozen highlands. Preferring solitude, this species does not form packs.
flavor.latest: Because of Sneasler's virulent poison and daunting physical prowess, no other species could hope to best it on the frozen highlands. Preferring solitude, this species does not form packs.

flavor.39: Its lancelike spikes and savage temperament have earned it the nickname ”sea fiend.” It slurps up poison to nourish itself.
flavor.latest: Its lancelike spikes and savage temperament have earned it the nickname ”sea fiend.” It slurps up poison to nourish itself.

flavor.39: When it flies to this land from across the sea, the bitter winter comes to an end. According to legend, this Pokémon's love gives rise to the budding of fresh life across Hisui.
flavor.latest: When it flies to this land from across the sea, the bitter winter comes to an end. According to legend, this Pokémon's love gives rise to the budding of fresh life across Hisui.

flavor.40: Its fluffy fur is similar in composition to plants. This Pokémon frequently washes its face to keep it from drying out.
flavor.41: The sweet scent its body gives off mesmerizes those around it. The scent grows stronger when this Pokémon is in the sun.
flavor.latest: Its fluffy fur is similar in composition to plants. This Pokémon frequently washes its face to keep it from drying out.

flavor.40: Floragato deftly wields the vine hidden beneath its long fur, slamming the hard flower bud against its opponents.

flavor.latest: Floragato deftly wields the vine hidden beneath its long fur, slamming the hard flower bud against its opponents.

flavor.40: This Pokémon uses the reflective fur lining its cape to camouflage the stem of its flower, creating the illusion that the flower is floating.
flavor.41: With skillful misdirection, it rigs foes with pollen-packed flower bombs. Meowscarada sets off the bombs before its foes realize what’s going on.
flavor.latest: This Pokémon uses the reflective fur lining its cape to camouflage the stem of its flower, creating the illusion that the flower is floating.

flavor.40: It lies on warm rocks and uses the heat absorbed by its square-shaped scales to create fire energy.
flavor.41: Its flame sac is small, so energy is always leaking out. This energy is released from the dent atop Fuecoco’s head and flickers to and fro.
flavor.latest: It lies on warm rocks and uses the heat absorbed by its square-shaped scales to create fire energy.

flavor.40: The combination of Crocalor’s fire energy and overflowing vitality has caused an egg-shaped fireball to appear on the Pokémon’s head.
flavor.41: The valve in Crocalor’s flame sac is closely connected to its vocal cords. This Pokémon utters a guttural cry as it spews flames every which way.
flavor.latest: The combination of Crocalor’s fire energy and overflowing vitality has caused an egg-shaped fireball to appear on the Pokémon’s head.

flavor.41: Skeledirge’s gentle singing soothes the souls of all that hear it. It burns its enemies to a crisp with flames of over 5,400 degrees Fahrenheit.
flavor.latest: The fiery bird changes shape when Skeledirge sings. Rumor has it that the bird was born when the fireball on Skeledirge’s head gained a soul.

flavor.40: This Pokémon migrated to Paldea from distant lands long ago. The gel secreted by its feathers repels water and grime.
flavor.41: Its strong legs let it easily swim around in even fast-flowing rivers. It likes to keep things tidy and is prone to overthinking things.
flavor.latest: This Pokémon migrated to Paldea from distant lands long ago. The gel secreted by its feathers repels water and grime.

flavor.40: These Pokémon constantly run through shallow waters to train their legs, then compete with each other to see which of them kicks most gracefully.
flavor.41: The hardworking Quaxwell observes people and Pokémon from various regions and incorporates their movements into its own dance routines.
flavor.latest: These Pokémon constantly run through shallow waters to train their legs, then compete with each other to see which of them kicks most gracefully.

flavor.40: A single kick from a Quaquaval can send a truck rolling. This Pokémon uses its powerful legs to perform striking dances from far-off lands.
flavor.41: Dancing in ways that evoke far-away places, this Pokémon mesmerizes all that see it. Flourishes of its decorative water feathers slice into its foes.
flavor.latest: A single kick from a Quaquaval can send a truck rolling. This Pokémon uses its powerful legs to perform striking dances from far-off lands.

flavor.40: It searches for food all day. It possesses a keen sense of smell but doesn’t use it for anything other than foraging.
flavor.41: This Pokémon spurns all but the finest of foods. Its body gives off an herblike scent that bug Pokémon detest.
flavor.latest: It searches for food all day. It possesses a keen sense of smell but doesn’t use it for anything other than foraging.

flavor.40: Oinkologne is proud of its fine, glossy skin. It emits a concentrated scent from the tip of its tail.
flavor.41: It entrances female Pokémon with the sweet, alluring scent that wafts from all over its body.
flavor.latest: Oinkologne is proud of its fine, glossy skin. It emits a concentrated scent from the tip of its tail.

flavor.40: The ball of threads wrapped around its body is elastic enough to deflect the scythes of Scyther, this Pokémon’s natural enemy.

flavor.latest: The ball of threads wrapped around its body is elastic enough to deflect the scythes of Scyther, this Pokémon’s natural enemy.

flavor.40: It clings to branches and ceilings using its threads and moves without a sound. It takes out its prey before the prey even notices it.

flavor.latest: It clings to branches and ceilings using its threads and moves without a sound. It takes out its prey before the prey even notices it.

flavor.latest: It has its third set of legs folded up. When it’s in a tough spot, this Pokémon jumps over 30 feet using the strength of its legs.

flavor.40: When it decides to fight all out, it stands on its previously folded legs to enter Showdown Mode. It neutralizes its enemies in short order.

flavor.latest: When it decides to fight all out, it stands on its previously folded legs to enter Showdown Mode. It neutralizes its enemies in short order.

flavor.40: This Pokémon normally is slow to react, but once it enters battle, it will strike down its enemies with lightning-fast movements.

flavor.latest: This Pokémon normally is slow to react, but once it enters battle, it will strike down its enemies with lightning-fast movements.

flavor.latest: The pleasant aroma that emanates from this Pokémon’s body helps wheat grow, so Dachsbun has been treasured by farming villages.

flavor.latest: This calm Pokémon is very compassionate. It will share its delicious, nutrient-rich oil with weakened Pokémon.

flavor.latest: Garganacl will rub its fingertips together and sprinkle injured Pokémon with salt. Even severe wounds will promptly heal afterward.

flavor.latest: The fiery blades on its arms burn fiercely with the lingering resentment of a sword wielder who fell before accomplishing their goal.

flavor.latest: Tadbulb shakes its tail to generate electricity. If it senses danger, it will make its head blink on and off to alert its allies.

flavor.latest: Kilowattrel inflates its throat sac to amplify its electricity. By riding the wind, this Pokémon can fly over 430 miles in a day.

flavor.41: Its well-developed jaw and fangs are strong enough to crunch through boulders, and its thick fat makes for an excellent defense.
flavor.latest: It always scowls in an attempt to make opponents take it seriously, but even crying children will burst into laughter when they see Maschiff’s face.

flavor.latest: This Pokémon can store energy in its large dewlap. Mabosstiff unleashes this energy all at once to blow away enemies.

flavor.40: Though usually a mellow Pokémon, it will sink its sharp, poison-soaked front teeth into any that anger it, causing paralysis in the object of its ire.
flavor.41: To keep enemies away from its territory, it paints markings around its nest using a poisonous liquid that has an acrid odor.
flavor.latest: Though usually a mellow Pokémon, it will sink its sharp, poison-soaked front teeth into any that anger it, causing paralysis in the object of its ire.

flavor.40: The color of the poisonous saliva depends on what the Pokémon eats. Grafaiai covers its fingers in its saliva and draws patterns on trees in forests.
flavor.41: Each Grafaiai paints its own individual pattern, and it will paint that same pattern over and over again throughout its life.
flavor.latest: The color of the poisonous saliva depends on what the Pokémon eats. Grafaiai covers its fingers in its saliva and draws patterns on trees in forests.

flavor.latest: A soul unable to move on to the afterlife was blown around by the wind until it got tangled up with dried grass and became a Pokémon.

flavor.40: It will open the branches of its head to envelop its prey. Once it absorbs all the life energy it needs, it expels the prey and discards it.

flavor.latest: It will open the branches of its head to envelop its prey. Once it absorbs all the life energy it needs, it expels the prey and discards it.

flavor.40: Toedscool lives in muggy forests. The flaps that fall from its body are chewy and very delicious.

flavor.latest: Toedscool lives in muggy forests. The flaps that fall from its body are chewy and very delicious.

flavor.40: These Pokémon gather into groups and form colonies deep within forests. They absolutely hate it when strangers approach.
flavor.41: It coils its 10 tentacles around prey and sucks out their nutrients, causing the prey pain. The folds along the rim of its head are a popular delicacy.
flavor.latest: These Pokémon gather into groups and form colonies deep within forests. They absolutely hate it when strangers approach.

flavor.40: Klawf hangs upside-down from cliffs, waiting for prey. But Klawf can’t remain in this position for long because its blood rushes to its head.
flavor.41: This Pokémon lives on sheer cliffs. It sidesteps opponents’ attacks, then lunges for their weak spots with its claws.
flavor.latest: Klawf hangs upside-down from cliffs, waiting for prey. But Klawf can’t remain in this position for long because its blood rushes to its head.

flavor.40: The more sunlight this Pokémon bathes in, the more spicy chemicals are produced by its body, and thus the spicier its moves become.

flavor.latest: The more sunlight this Pokémon bathes in, the more spicy chemicals are produced by its body, and thus the spicier its moves become.

flavor.latest: The red head converts spicy chemicals into fire energy and blasts the surrounding area with a super spicy stream of flame.

flavor.latest: This Pokémon creates a mud ball by mixing sand and dirt with psychic energy. It treasures its mud ball more than its own life.

flavor.40: The body that supports the ball barely moves. Therefore, it is thought that the true body of this Pokémon is actually inside the ball.

flavor.latest: The body that supports the ball barely moves. Therefore, it is thought that the true body of this Pokémon is actually inside the ball.

flavor.40: Flittle’s toes levitate about half an inch above the ground because of the psychic power emitted from the frills on the Pokémon’s belly.

flavor.latest: Flittle’s toes levitate about half an inch above the ground because of the psychic power emitted from the frills on the Pokémon’s belly.

flavor.latest: It immobilizes opponents by bathing them in psychic power from its large eyes. Despite its appearance, it has a vicious temperament.

flavor.latest: It swings its handmade hammer around to protect itself, but the hammer is often stolen by Pokémon that eat metal.

flavor.latest: This Pokémon will attack groups of Pawniard and Bisharp, gathering metal from them in order to create a large and sturdy hammer.

flavor.latest: This intelligent Pokémon has a very daring disposition. It knocks rocks into the sky with its hammer, aiming for flying Corviknight.

flavor.40: This Pokémon can pick up the scent of a Veluza just over 65 feet away and will hide itself in the sand.
flavor.41: Though it looks like Diglett, Wiglett is an entirely different species. The resemblance seems to be a coincidental result of environmental adaptation.
flavor.latest: This Pokémon can pick up the scent of a Veluza just over 65 feet away and will hide itself in the sand.

flavor.40: It has a vicious temperament, contrary to what its appearance may suggest. It wraps its long bodies around prey, then drags the prey into its den.
flavor.41: A variety of fish Pokémon, Wugtrio was once considered to be a regional form of Dugtrio.
flavor.latest: It has a vicious temperament, contrary to what its appearance may suggest. It wraps its long bodies around prey, then drags the prey into its den.

flavor.40: It gathers things up in an apron made from shed feathers added to the Pokémon’s chest feathers, then drops those things from high places for fun.
flavor.41: Bombirdier uses the apron on its chest to bundle up food, which it carries back to its nest. It enjoys dropping things that make loud noises.
flavor.latest: It gathers things up in an apron made from shed feathers added to the Pokémon’s chest feathers, then drops those things from high places for fun.

flavor.40: It likes playing with others of its kind using the water ring on its tail. It uses ultrasonic waves to sense the emotions of other living creatures.
flavor.41: Its water ring is made from seawater mixed with a sticky fluid that Finizen secretes from its blowhole.
flavor.latest: It likes playing with others of its kind using the water ring on its tail. It uses ultrasonic waves to sense the emotions of other living creatures.

flavor.40: This Pokémon changes its appearance if it hears its allies calling for help. Palafin will never show anybody its moment of transformation.
flavor.41: Its physical capabilities are no different than a Finizen’s, but when its allies are in danger, it transforms and powers itself up.
flavor.latest: This Pokémon changes its appearance if it hears its allies calling for help. Palafin will never show anybody its moment of transformation.

flavor.40: It is said that this Pokémon was born when an unknown poison Pokémon entered and inspirited an engine left at a scrap-processing factory.
flavor.41: The steel section is Varoom’s actual body. This Pokémon clings to rocks and converts the minerals within into energy to fuel its activities.
flavor.latest: It is said that this Pokémon was born when an unknown poison Pokémon entered and inspirited an engine left at a scrap-processing factory.

flavor.40: It creates a gas out of poison and minerals from rocks. It then detonates the gas in its cylinders—now numbering eight—to generate energy.
flavor.41: Revavroom viciously threatens others with the sound of its exhaust. It sticks its tongue out from its cylindrical mouth and sprays toxic fluids.
flavor.latest: It creates a gas out of poison and minerals from rocks. It then detonates the gas in its cylinders—now numbering eight—to generate energy.

flavor.40: Apparently Cyclizar has been allowing people to ride on its back since ancient times. Depictions of this have been found in 10,000-year-old murals.
flavor.41: It can sprint at over 70 mph while carrying a human. The rider’s body heat warms Cyclizar’s back and lifts the Pokémon’s spirit.
flavor.latest: Apparently Cyclizar has been allowing people to ride on its back since ancient times. Depictions of this have been found in 10,000-year-old murals.

flavor.40: When attacked, this Pokémon will wield the tendrils on its body like fists and pelt the opponent with a storm of punches.
flavor.41: This Pokémon lives in arid deserts. It maintains its metal body by consuming iron from the soil.
flavor.latest: When attacked, this Pokémon will wield the tendrils on its body like fists and pelt the opponent with a storm of punches.

flavor.40: It absorbs nutrients from cave walls. The petals it wears are made of crystallized poison.
flavor.41: Glimmet’s toxic mineral crystals look just like flower petals. This Pokémon scatters poisonous powder like pollen to protect itself.
flavor.latest: It absorbs nutrients from cave walls. The petals it wears are made of crystallized poison.

flavor.40: When this Pokémon detects danger, it will open up its crystalline petals and fire beams from its conical body.
flavor.41: Glimmora’s petals are made of crystallized poison energy. It has recently become evident that these petals resemble Tera Jewels.
flavor.latest: When this Pokémon detects danger, it will open up its crystalline petals and fire beams from its conical body.

flavor.40: It is said that a dog Pokémon that died in the wild without ever interacting with a human was reborn as this Pokémon.
flavor.41: This friendly Pokémon doesn’t like being alone. Pay it even the slightest bit of attention, and it will follow you forever.
flavor.latest: It is said that a dog Pokémon that died in the wild without ever interacting with a human was reborn as this Pokémon.

flavor.40: Houndstone spends most of its time sleeping in graveyards. Among all the dog Pokémon, this one is most loyal to its master.
flavor.41: A lovingly mourned Pokémon was reborn as Houndstone. It doesn’t like anyone touching the protuberance atop its head.
flavor.latest: Houndstone spends most of its time sleeping in graveyards. Among all the dog Pokémon, this one is most loyal to its master.

flavor.40: This Pokémon apparently ties the base of its neck into a knot so that energy stored in its belly does not escape from its beak.
flavor.41: Thanks to a behavior of theirs known as “synchronizing,” an entire flock of these Pokémon can attack simultaneously in perfect harmony.
flavor.latest: This Pokémon apparently ties the base of its neck into a knot so that energy stored in its belly does not escape from its beak.

flavor.40: This species left the ocean and began living on land a very long time ago. It seems to be closely related to Wailmer.
flavor.41: It lives in frigid regions in pods of five or so individuals. It loves the minerals found in snow and ice.
flavor.latest: This species left the ocean and began living on land a very long time ago. It seems to be closely related to Wailmer.

flavor.40: This Pokémon wanders around snowy, icy areas. It protects its body with powerful muscles and a thick layer of fat under its skin.
flavor.41: Ice energy builds up in the horn on its upper jaw, causing the horn to reach cryogenic temperatures that freeze its surroundings.
flavor.latest: This Pokémon wanders around snowy, icy areas. It protects its body with powerful muscles and a thick layer of fat under its skin.

flavor.40: When Veluza discards unnecessary flesh, its mind becomes honed and its psychic power increases. The spare flesh has a mild but delicious flavor.
flavor.41: Veluza has excellent regenerative capabilities. It sheds spare flesh from its body to boost its agility, then charges at its prey.
flavor.latest: When Veluza discards unnecessary flesh, its mind becomes honed and its psychic power increases. The spare flesh has a mild but delicious flavor.

flavor.40: This Pokémon is a glutton, but it’s bad at getting food. It teams up with a Tatsugiri to catch prey.
flavor.41: It treats Tatsugiri like its boss and follows it loyally. Though powerful, Dondozo is apparently not very smart.
flavor.latest: This Pokémon is a glutton, but it’s bad at getting food. It teams up with a Tatsugiri to catch prey.

flavor.40: This is a small dragon Pokémon. It lives inside the mouth of Dondozo to protect itself from enemies on the outside.
flavor.41: Tatsugiri is an extremely cunning Pokémon. It feigns weakness to lure in prey, then orders its partner to attack.
flavor.latest: This is a small dragon Pokémon. It lives inside the mouth of Dondozo to protect itself from enemies on the outside.

flavor.40: When its anger rose beyond a critical point, this Pokémon gained power that is unfettered by the limits of its physical body.
flavor.41: It imbues its fists with the power of the rage that it kept hidden in its heart. Opponents struck by these imbued fists will be shattered to their core.
flavor.latest: When its anger rose beyond a critical point, this Pokémon gained power that is unfettered by the limits of its physical body.

flavor.40: When attacked, this Pokémon will retaliate by sticking thick spines out from its body. It’s a risky move that puts everything on the line.
flavor.41: It lives at the bottom of ponds and swamps. It will carry Wooper on its back and ferry them across water from one shore to the other.
flavor.latest: When attacked, this Pokémon will retaliate by sticking thick spines out from its body. It’s a risky move that puts everything on the line.

flavor.40: Now that the brain waves from the head and tail are synced up, the psychic power of this Pokémon is 10 times stronger than Girafarig’s.
flavor.41: The hardened head from the tail protects the head of the main body as Farigiraf whips its long neck around to headbutt enemies.
flavor.latest: Now that the brain waves from the head and tail are synced up, the psychic power of this Pokémon is 10 times stronger than Girafarig’s.

flavor.40: This Pokémon uses its hard tail to make its nest by boring holes into bedrock deep underground. The nest can reach lengths of over six miles.
flavor.41: It drives enemies out of its nest by sucking in enough air to fill its long, narrow lungs, then releasing the air in an intense blast.
flavor.latest: This Pokémon uses its hard tail to make its nest by boring holes into bedrock deep underground. The nest can reach lengths of over six miles.

flavor.40: Only a Bisharp that stands above all others in its vast army can evolve into Kingambit.
flavor.41: Though it commands a massive army in battle, it’s not skilled at devising complex strategies. It just uses brute strength to keep pushing.
flavor.latest: Only a Bisharp that stands above all others in its vast army can evolve into Kingambit.

flavor.40: Sightings of this Pokémon have occurred in recent years. The name Great Tusk was taken from a creature listed in a certain book.
flavor.41: This creature resembles a mysterious Pokémon that, according to a paranormal magazine, has lived since ancient times.
flavor.latest: Sightings of this Pokémon have occurred in recent years. The name Great Tusk was taken from a creature listed in a certain book.

flavor.40: There has been only one reported sighting of this Pokémon. It resembles a mysterious creature depicted in an old expedition journal.
flavor.41: It resembles a mysterious Pokémon described in a paranormal magazine as a Jigglypuff from one billion years ago.
flavor.latest: There has been only one reported sighting of this Pokémon. It resembles a mysterious creature depicted in an old expedition journal.

flavor.40: It is possible that the creature listed as Brute Bonnet in a certain book could actually be this Pokémon.
flavor.41: It bears a slight resemblance to a Pokémon described in a dubious magazine as a cross between a dinosaur and a mushroom.
flavor.latest: It is possible that the creature listed as Brute Bonnet in a certain book could actually be this Pokémon.

flavor.40: This Pokémon has characteristics similar to those of Flutter Mane, a creature mentioned in a certain book.
flavor.41: It has similar features to a ghostly pterosaur that was covered in a paranormal magazine, but the two have little else in common.
flavor.latest: This Pokémon has characteristics similar to those of Flutter Mane, a creature mentioned in a certain book.

flavor.40: This mysterious Pokémon has some similarities to a creature that an old book introduced as Slither Wing.
flavor.41: This Pokémon somewhat resembles an ancient form of Volcarona that was introduced in a dubious magazine.
flavor.latest: This mysterious Pokémon has some similarities to a creature that an old book introduced as Slither Wing.

flavor.40: No records exist of this Pokémon being caught. Data is lacking, but the Pokémon’s traits match up with a creature shown in an expedition journal.
flavor.41: It slightly resembles a Magneton that lived for 10,000 years and was featured in an article in a paranormal magazine.
flavor.latest: No records exist of this Pokémon being caught. Data is lacking, but the Pokémon’s traits match up with a creature shown in an expedition journal.

flavor.40: This Pokémon closely resembles a scientific weapon that a paranormal magazine claimed was sent to this planet by aliens.
flavor.41: Sightings of this Pokémon have occurred in recent years. It resembles a mysterious object described in an old expedition journal.
flavor.latest: This Pokémon closely resembles a scientific weapon that a paranormal magazine claimed was sent to this planet by aliens.

flavor.40: Its shape is similar to a robot featured in a paranormal magazine article. The robot was said to have been created by an ancient civilization.
flavor.41: It resembles a mysterious object mentioned in an old book. There are only two reported sightings of this Pokémon.
flavor.latest: Its shape is similar to a robot featured in a paranormal magazine article. The robot was said to have been created by an ancient civilization.

flavor.40: It is very similar to a cyborg covered exclusively by a paranormal magazine. The cyborg was said to be the modified form of a certain athlete.
flavor.41: This Pokémon shares many similarities with Iron Hands, an object mentioned in a certain expedition journal.
flavor.latest: It is very similar to a cyborg covered exclusively by a paranormal magazine. The cyborg was said to be the modified form of a certain athlete.

flavor.40: It resembles a certain Pokémon introduced in a paranormal magazine, described as the offspring of a Hydreigon that fell in love with a robot.
flavor.41: It’s possible that Iron Jugulis, an object described in an old book, may actually be this Pokémon.
flavor.latest: It resembles a certain Pokémon introduced in a paranormal magazine, described as the offspring of a Hydreigon that fell in love with a robot.

flavor.40: This Pokémon resembles an unknown object described in a paranormal magazine as a UFO sent to observe humanity.
flavor.41: No records exist of this species being caught. Data is lacking, but the Pokémon’s traits match up with an object described in an old book.
flavor.latest: This Pokémon resembles an unknown object described in a paranormal magazine as a UFO sent to observe humanity.

flavor.40: It has some similarities to a Pokémon introduced in a dubious magazine as a Tyranitar from one billion years into the future.
flavor.41: Some of its notable features match those of an object named within a certain expedition journal as Iron Thorns.
flavor.latest: It has some similarities to a Pokémon introduced in a dubious magazine as a Tyranitar from one billion years into the future.

flavor.40: Frigibax absorbs heat through its dorsal fin and converts the heat into ice energy. The higher the temperature, the more energy Frigibax stores.
flavor.41: This Pokémon lives in forests and craggy areas. Using the power of its dorsal fin, it cools the inside of its nest like a refrigerator.
flavor.latest: Frigibax absorbs heat through its dorsal fin and converts the heat into ice energy. The higher the temperature, the more energy Frigibax stores.

flavor.40: Arctibax freezes the air around it, protecting its face with an ice mask and turning its dorsal fin into a blade of ice.
flavor.41: It attacks with the blade of its frozen dorsal fin by doing a front flip in the air. Arctibax’s strong back and legs allow it to pull off this technique.
flavor.latest: Arctibax freezes the air around it, protecting its face with an ice mask and turning its dorsal fin into a blade of ice.

flavor.40: This Pokémon blasts cryogenic air out from its mouth. This air can instantly freeze even liquid-hot lava.
flavor.41: It launches itself into battle by flipping upside down and spewing frigid air from its mouth. It finishes opponents off with its dorsal blade.
flavor.latest: This Pokémon blasts cryogenic air out from its mouth. This air can instantly freeze even liquid-hot lava.

flavor.40: This Pokémon was born inside a treasure chest about 1,500 years ago. It sucks the life-force out of scoundrels who try to steal the treasure.
flavor.41: It lives inside an old treasure chest. Sometimes it gets left in shop corners since no one realizes it’s actually a Pokémon.
flavor.latest: This Pokémon was born inside a treasure chest about 1,500 years ago. It sucks the life-force out of scoundrels who try to steal the treasure.

flavor.40: Its body seems to be made up of 1,000 coins. This Pokémon gets along well with others and is quick to make friends with anybody.
flavor.41: It has a sturdy body made up of stacked coins. Gholdengo overwhelms its enemies by firing coin after coin at them in quick succession.
flavor.latest: Its body seems to be made up of 1,000 coins. This Pokémon gets along well with others and is quick to make friends with anybody.

flavor.40: The grudge of a person punished for writing the king’s evil deeds upon wooden tablets has clad itself in dead leaves to become a Pokémon.
flavor.41: It drains the life-force from vegetation, causing nearby forests to instantly wither and fields to turn barren.
flavor.latest: The grudge of a person punished for writing the king’s evil deeds upon wooden tablets has clad itself in dead leaves to become a Pokémon.

flavor.40: This Pokémon can control 100 tons of fallen snow. It plays around innocently by leaping in and out of avalanches it has caused.
flavor.41: The hatred of those who perished by the sword long ago has clad itself in snow and become a Pokémon.
flavor.latest: This Pokémon can control 100 tons of fallen snow. It plays around innocently by leaping in and out of avalanches it has caused.

flavor.40: The fear poured into an ancient ritual vessel has clad itself in rocks and dirt to become a Pokémon.
flavor.41: It slowly brings its exceedingly heavy head down upon the ground, splitting the earth open with huge fissures that run over 160 feet deep.
flavor.latest: The fear poured into an ancient ritual vessel has clad itself in rocks and dirt to become a Pokémon.

flavor.40: It controls flames burning at over 5,400 degrees Fahrenheit. It casually swims through the sea of lava it creates by melting rock and sand.
flavor.41: The envy accumulated within curved beads that sparked multiple conflicts has clad itself in fire and become a Pokémon.
flavor.latest: It controls flames burning at over 5,400 degrees Fahrenheit. It casually swims through the sea of lava it creates by melting rock and sand.

flavor.40: It is possible that this is the creature listed as Roaring Moon in an expedition journal that still holds many mysteries.
flavor.41: According to an article in a dubious magazine, this Pokémon has some connection to a phenomenon that occurs in a certain region.
flavor.latest: It is possible that this is the creature listed as Roaring Moon in an expedition journal that still holds many mysteries.

flavor.40: It has some similarities to a mad scientist’s invention covered in a paranormal magazine.
flavor.41: It’s possible that this is the object listed as Iron Valiant in a certain expedition journal.
flavor.latest: It has some similarities to a mad scientist’s invention covered in a paranormal magazine.

flavor.40: This seems to be the Winged King mentioned in an old expedition journal. It was said to have split the land with its bare fists.
flavor.41: This Pokémon resembles Cyclizar, but it is far burlier and more ferocious. Nothing is known about its ecology or other features.
flavor.latest: This seems to be the Winged King mentioned in an old expedition journal. It was said to have split the land with its bare fists.

flavor.40: Much remains unknown about this creature. It resembles Cyclizar, but it is far more ruthless and powerful.
flavor.41: This seems to be the Iron Serpent mentioned in an old book. The Iron Serpent is said to have turned the land to ash with its lightning.
flavor.latest: Much remains unknown about this creature. It resembles Cyclizar, but it is far more ruthless and powerful.

flavor.40: This ferocious creature is shrouded in mystery. It's named after an aquatic monster mentioned in an old expedition journal.
flavor.41: It resembles an illustration published in a paranormal magazine, said to be a depiction of a super-ancient Suicune.
flavor.latest: This ferocious creature is shrouded in mystery. It's named after an aquatic monster mentioned in an old expedition journal.

flavor.40: Many of its physical characteristics match those of a Virizion from the future that was covered in a paranormal magazine.
flavor.41: According to the few eyewitness accounts that exist, it used its shining blades to julienne large trees and boulders.
flavor.latest: Many of its physical characteristics match those of a Virizion from the future that was covered in a paranormal magazine.

flavor.40: Dipplin is two creatures in one Pokémon. Its evolution was triggered by a special apple grown only in one place.
flavor.41: The head sticking out belongs to the fore-wyrm, while the tail belongs to the core-wyrm. The two share one apple and help each other out.
flavor.latest: Dipplin is two creatures in one Pokémon. Its evolution was triggered by a special apple grown only in one place.

flavor.40: Supposedly, the regrets of a tea ceremony master who died before perfecting his craft lingered in some matcha and became a Pokémon.
flavor.41: Poltchageist looks like a regional form of Sinistea, but it was recently discovered that the two Pokémon are entirely unrelated.
flavor.latest: Supposedly, the regrets of a tea ceremony master who died before perfecting his craft lingered in some matcha and became a Pokémon.

flavor.40: It pretends to be tea, trying to fool people into drinking it so it can drain their life-force. Its ruse is generally unsuccessful.
flavor.41: It prefers cool, dark places, such as the back of a shelf or the space beneath a home's floorboards. It wanders in search of prey after sunset.
flavor.latest: It pretends to be tea, trying to fool people into drinking it so it can drain their life-force. Its ruse is generally unsuccessful.

flavor.40: After all its muscles were stimulated by the toxic chain around its neck, Okidogi transformed and gained a powerful physique.
flavor.41: Okidogi is a ruffian with a short temper. It can pulverize anything by swinging around the chain on its neck.
flavor.latest: After all its muscles were stimulated by the toxic chain around its neck, Okidogi transformed and gained a powerful physique.

flavor.40: The chain is made from toxins that enhance capabilities. It stimulated Munkidori's brain and caused the Pokémon's psychic powers to bloom.
flavor.41: Munkidori keeps itself somewhere safe while it toys with its foes, using psychokinesis to induce intense dizziness.
flavor.latest: The chain is made from toxins that enhance capabilities. It stimulated Munkidori's brain and caused the Pokémon's psychic powers to bloom.

flavor.40: Fezandipiti owes its beautiful looks and lovely voice to the toxic stimulants emanating from the chain wrapped around its body.
flavor.41: Fezandipiti beats its glossy wings to scatter pheromones that captivate people and Pokémon.
flavor.latest: Fezandipiti owes its beautiful looks and lovely voice to the toxic stimulants emanating from the chain wrapped around its body.

flavor.40: This Pokémon's type changes based on which mask it's wearing. It confounds its enemies with nimble movements and kicks.
flavor.41: This mischief-loving Pokémon is full of curiosity. It battles by drawing out the type-based energy contained within its masks.
flavor.latest: This Pokémon's type changes based on which mask it's wearing. It confounds its enemies with nimble movements and kicks.

flavor.40: It gathers static electricity from its surroundings. The beams it launches when down on all fours are tremendously powerful.
flavor.41: It digs holes on mountains, searching for food. It’s so durable that being caught in a cave-in won’t faze it.
flavor.latest: It gathers static electricity from its surroundings. The beams it launches when down on all fours are tremendously powerful.

flavor.40: Seven syrpents live inside an apple made of syrup. The syrpent in the center is the commander.
flavor.41: These capricious syrpents have banded together. On the rare occasion that their moods align, their true power is unleashed.
flavor.latest: Seven syrpents live inside an apple made of syrup. The syrpent in the center is the commander.

flavor.40: There are scant few reports of this creature being sighted. One short video shows it rampaging and spouting pillars of flame.
flavor.41: It resembles an eerie Pokémon once shown in a paranormal magazine. That Pokémon was said to be an Entei regenerated from a fossil.
flavor.latest: There are scant few reports of this creature being sighted. One short video shows it rampaging and spouting pillars of flame.

flavor.40: It's said to incinerate everything around it with lightning launched from its fur. Very little is known about this creature.
flavor.41: It bears resemblance to a Pokémon that became a hot topic for a short while after a paranormal magazine touted it as Raikou's ancestor.
flavor.latest: It's said to incinerate everything around it with lightning launched from its fur. Very little is known about this creature.

flavor.40: It resembles a Pokémon described in a dubious magazine as a Terrakion that had been modified by an evil organization.
flavor.41: It was named after a mysterious object recorded in an old book. Its body seems to be metallic.
flavor.latest: It resembles a Pokémon described in a dubious magazine as a Terrakion that had been modified by an evil organization.

flavor.40: It resembles a mysterious object introduced in a paranormal magazine as a cutting-edge weapon shaped like a Cobalion.
flavor.41: There was supposedly an incident in which it launched shining blades to cut everything around it to pieces. Little else is known about it.
flavor.latest: It resembles a mysterious object introduced in a paranormal magazine as a cutting-edge weapon shaped like a Cobalion.

flavor.40: Terapagos protects itself using its power to transform energy into hard crystals. This Pokémon is the source of the Terastal phenomenon.
flavor.41: It’s thought that this Pokémon lived in ancient Paldea until it got caught in seismic shifts and went extinct.
flavor.latest: Terapagos protects itself using its power to transform energy into hard crystals. This Pokémon is the source of the Terastal phenomenon.

flavor.40: It feeds others toxic mochi that draw out desires and capabilities. Those who eat the mochi fall under Pecharunt’s control, chained to its will.
flavor.41: Its peach-shaped shell serves as storage for a potent poison. It makes poisonous mochi and serves them to people and Pokémon.
flavor.latest: It feeds others toxic mochi that draw out desires and capabilities. Those who eat the mochi fall under Pecharunt’s control, chained to its will.

moves.effect: Inflicts regular damage.

moves.short: Has an increased chance for a critical hit.
moves.effect: Inflicts regular damage. User’s critical hit rate is one level higher when using this move.
flavor: Has a high critical hit ratio.
A chopping attack with a high critical-hit ratio.
The foe is attacked with a sharp chop. It has a high critical-hit ratio.
The target is attacked with a sharp chop. Critical hits land more easily.

moves.short: Hits 2-5 times in one turn.
moves.effect:
Inflicts regular damage. Hits 2–5 times in one turn.

Has a 3/8 chance each to hit 2 or 3 times, and a 1/8 chance each to hit 4 or 5 times. Averages to 3 hits per use.

Repeatedly slaps the foe 2 to 5 times.

moves.effect: Inflicts regular damage.

The target is slugged by a punch thrown with muscle-packed power.

moves.short: Scatters money on the ground worth five times the user’s level.
moves.effect: Inflicts regular damage. After the battle ends, the winner receives five times the user’s level in extra money for each time this move was used.
flavor: Throws coins. Gets them back later.
Throws coins at the foe. Money is recovered after.
Numerous coins are hurled at the foe. Money is earned after battle.
Numerous coins are hurled at the foe to inflict damage. Money is earned after battle.
Numerous coins are hurled at the target to inflict damage. Money is earned after the battle.
Coins are hurled at the target to inflict damage. Money is earned after the battle.

moves.effect: Inflicts regular damage. Has a chance to burn the target.

The target is punched with a fiery fist. It may also leave the target with a burn.

moves.short: Has a chance to freeze the target.
moves.effect: Inflicts regular damage. Has a chance to freeze the target.
flavor: An icy punch. May cause freezing.
An icy punch that may freeze the foe.
The foe is punched with an icy fist. It may leave the foe frozen.
The foe is punched with an icy fist. It may leave the target frozen.
The target is punched with an icy fist. It may also leave the target frozen.
The target is punched with an icy fist. This may also leave the target frozen.
The target is punched with an icy fist. This may also leave the target with frostbite.

moves.short: Has a chance to paralyze the target.
moves.effect: Inflicts regular damage. Has a chance to paralyze the target.

An electrified punch that may paralyze the foe.

The foe is punched with an electrified fist. It may leave the target with paralysis.

moves.name: Substitute
moves.short: Transfers 1/4 of the user’s max HP into a doll, protecting the user from further damage or status changes until it breaks.
moves.effect:
Transfers 1/4 the user’s max HP into a doll that absorbs damage and causes most negative move effects to fail. If the user leaves the field, the doll will vanish. If the user cannot pay the HP cost, this move will fail.

The doll takes damage as normal, using the user’s stats and types, and will break when its HP reaches zero. Self-inflicted damage from confusion or recoil is not absorbed. Healing effects from opponents ignore the doll and heal the user as normal. Moves that work based on the user’s HP still do so; the doll’s HP does not influence any move.

The doll will block major status effects, confusion, and flinching. The effects of Smelling Salts and Wake-Up Slap do not trigger against a doll, even if the Pokémon behind the doll has the appropriate major status effect. Multi-turn trapping moves like Wrap will hit the doll for their regular damage, but the multi-turn trapping and damage effects will not activate.

Moves blocked or damage absorbed by the doll do not count as hitting the user or inflicting damage for any effects that respond to such, e.g., Avalanche, Counter, or a Rowap Berry. Magic Coat still works as normal, even against moves the doll would block. Opposing Pokémon that damage the doll with a leech move like Absorb are healed as normal.

It will also block Acupressure, Block, the curse effect of Curse, Dream Eater, Embargo, Flatter, Gastro Acid, Grudge, Heal Block, Leech Seed, Lock-On, Mean Look, Mimic, Mind Reader, Nightmare, Pain Split, Psycho Shift, Spider Web, Sketch, Swagger, Switcheroo, Trick, Worry Seed, and Yawn. A Pokémon affected by Yawn before summoning the doll will still fall to sleep.

The doll blocks Intimidate, but all other abilities act as though the doll did not exist. If the user has an ability that absorbs moves of a certain type for HP (such as Volt Absorb absorbing Thunder Wave), such moves will not be blocked.

Life Orb and berries that cause confusion still work as normal, but their respective HP loss and confusion are absorbed/blocked by the doll.

The user is still vulnerable to damage inflicted when entering or leaving the field, such as by Pursuit or Spikes; however, the doll will block the poison effect of Toxic Spikes.

The doll is passed on by Baton Pass. It keeps its existing HP, but uses the replacement Pokémon’s stats and types for damage calculation.

All other effects work as normal.

moves.name: Hidden Power
moves.short: Power and type depend upon user’s IVs. Power can range from 30 to 70.
moves.effect:
Inflicts regular damage. Power and type are determined by the user’s IVs.

Power is given by `x * 40 / 63 + 30`. `x` is obtained by arranging bit 1 from the IV for each of Special Defense, Special Attack, Speed, Defense, Attack, and HP in that order. (Bit 1 is 1 if the IV is of the form `4n + 2` or `4n + 3`. `x` is then 64 * Special Defense IV bit 1, plus 32 * Special Attack IV bit 1, etc.)

Power is always between 30 and 70, inclusive. Average power is 49.5.

Type is given by `y * 15 / 63`, where `y` is similar to `x` above, except constructed from bit 0. (Bit 0 is 1 if the IV is odd.) The result is looked up in the following table.

Value | Type
----: | --------
 0 | Fighting
 1 | Flying
 2 | Poison
 3 | Ground
 4 | Rock
 5 | Bug
 6 | Ghost
 7 | Steel
 8 | Fire
 9 | Water
 10 | Grass
 11 | Electric
 12 | Psychic
 13 | Ice
 14 | Dragon
 15 | Dark

This move thus cannot be Normal. Most other types have an equal 1/16 chance to be selected, given random IVs. However, due to the flooring used here, Bug, Fighting, and Grass appear 5/64 of the time, and Dark only 1/64 of the time.

Every second turn on which this Pokémon should attempt to use a move, it will instead do nothing ("loaf around").

Loafing around interrupts moves that take multiple turns the same way paralysis, flinching, etc do. Most such moves, for example Bide or Rollout, are simply cut off upon loafing around. Attacks with a recharge turn, such as Hyper Beam, do not have to recharge; attacks with a preparation turn, such as Fly, do not end up being used. Moves that are forced over multiple turns and keep going through failure, such as Outrage, Uproar, or any move forced by Encore, keep going as usual.

If this Pokémon is confused, its confusion is not checked when loafing around; the Pokémon cannot hurt itself, and its confusion does not end or come closer to ending.

If this Pokémon attempts to move but fails, e.g. because of paralysis or Gravity, it still counts as having moved and will loaf around the next turn. If it does not attempt to move, e.g. because it is asleep or frozen, whatever it would have done will be postponed until its next attempt; that is, it will either loaf around or move as usual, depending on what it last did.

This ability cannot be changed with Worry Seed, but it can be disabled with Gastro Acid, changed with Role Play, or traded away with Skill Swap.

For example, this Pokémon's moves ignore abilities that would fully negate them, such as Water Absorb; abilities that would prevent any of their effects, such as Clear Body, Shell Armor, or Sticky Hold; and abilities that grant any general protective benefit, such as Simple, Snow Cloak, or Thick Fat. If an ability could either hinder or help this Pokémon's moves, e.g. Dry Skin or Unaware, the ability is ignored either way.

Abilities that do not fit this description, even if they could hinder moves in some other way, are not affected. For example, Cursed Body only affects potential future uses of the move, while Liquid Ooze and Shadow Tag can only hinder a move's effect on the user. This ablity cannot ignore type or form changes granted by abilities, for example Color Change or Forecast; nor effects that were caused by abilities but are no longer tied to an ability, such as the rain from Drizzle. This ability cannot ignore Multitype at all.

An ability ignored by this ability is only nullified while the move is being used. For example, this Pokémon's moves can paralyze a Pokémon with Limber, but Limber will activate and heal the paralysis immediately thereafter, and this Pokémon's Spikes are not affected by this ability after they have been placed.

When this Pokémon enters battle, all participating trainers are notified that it has this ability.

This ability functions identically to Teravolt and Turboblaze.

abilities.name: Turboblaze
abilities.short: Bypasses targets' abilities if they could hinder or prevent moves.
abilities.effect:
This Pokémon's moves completely ignore abilities that could hinder or prevent their effect on the target.

For example, this Pokémon's moves ignore abilities that would fully negate them, such as Water Absorb; abilities that would prevent any of their effects, such as Clear Body, Shell Armor, or Sticky Hold; and abilities that grant any general protective benefit, such as Simple, Snow Cloak, or Thick Fat. If an ability could either hinder or help this Pokémon's moves, e.g. Dry Skin or Unaware, the ability is ignored either way.

Abilities that do not fit this description, even if they could hinder moves in some other way, are not affected. For example, Cursed Body only affects potential future uses of the move, while Liquid Ooze and Shadow Tag can only hinder a move's effect on the user. This ablity cannot ignore type or form changes granted by abilities, for example Color Change or Forecast; nor effects that were caused by abilities but are no longer tied to an ability, such as the rain from Drizzle. This ability cannot ignore Multitype at all.

An ability ignored by this ability is only nullified while the move is being used. For example, this Pokémon's moves can paralyze a Pokémon with Limber, but Limber will activate and heal the paralysis immediately thereafter, and this Pokémon's Spikes are not affected by this ability after they have been placed.

When this Pokémon enters battle, all participating trainers are notified that it has this ability.

This ability functions identically to Mold Breaker and Teravolt.
flavor: Moves can be used regardless of Abilities.
Moves can be used on the target regardless of its Abilities.
The Pokémon's moves are unimpeded by the Ability of the target.

items.name: Surge Badge
flavor: A novelty badge that you can receive at the Kantonian Gym. Rumor has it that it imitates the Badge of a Gym somewhere.

flavor: A machine to fuse Necrozma, which needs light, and Solgaleo.

items.name: N-Lunarizer

items.name: N-Lunarizer

items.name: Ilima Normalium Z
flavor: The Normalium Z you were entrusted with by Ilima. You were asked to place it on the pedestal at the back of Verdant Cavern.

items.name: Left Poké Ball
flavor: A Poké Ball with a Pokémon that lost its Trainer inside. It seems to be from Ula’ula Island.

items.name: Roto Hatch
flavor: One of the Rotom Powers. It helps Eggs hatch faster.

items.name: Roto Bargain
flavor: One of the Rotom Powers. It reduces the prices of products at Poké Marts by half.

items.name: Roto Prize Money
flavor: One of the Rotom Powers. It triples the prize money you receive after battle.

items.name: Roto Exp. Points
flavor: One of the Rotom Powers. It increases the Exp. Points your Pokémon receive after battle a little.

items.name: Roto Friendship
flavor: One of the Rotom Powers. It helps Pokémon in your party grow friendly faster.

items.name: Roto Encounter
flavor: One of the Rotom Powers. It increases the chance of encountering high-level wild Pokémon a lot for a certain period of time.

items.name: Roto Stealth
flavor: One of the Rotom Powers. It prevents you from encountering wild Pokémon for a certain period of time.

items.name: Roto HP Restore
flavor: One of the Rotom Powers. It fully restores the HP of your battling Pokémon.

items.name: Roto PP Restore
flavor: One of the Rotom Powers. It fully restores the PP of your battling Pokémon.

items.name: Roto Boost
flavor: One of the Rotom Powers. It raises all stats of your battling Pokémon.

items.name: Roto Catch
flavor: One of the Rotom Powers. It increases the chance to catch Pokémon a lot.

items.name: Autograph
flavor: The autograph you got from the Vermilion City Gym Leader, Lt. Surge. He wrote, “Good luck!”

items.name: Clothing Trunk
flavor: A very light trunk that can carry clothing for you and your Pokémon.

items.name: Silver Razz Berry
flavor: A Berry that makes it easier to catch Pokémon when given to them.

items.name: Golden Razz Berry
flavor: A Berry that makes it drastically easier to catch Pokémon when given to them.

items.name: Silver Nanab Berry
flavor: A Berry that calms wild Pokémon you’re trying to catch when given to them.

items.name: Golden Nanab Berry
flavor: A Berry that calms wild Pokémon you’re trying to catch drastically when given to them.

items.name: Silver Pinap Berry
flavor: A Berry that makes you more likely to get an item when given to Pokémon you’re trying to catch.

items.name: Golden Pinap Berry
flavor: A Berry that makes you drastically more likely to get an item when given to Pokémon you’re trying to catch.

items.name: Secret Key
flavor: The key that unlocks the front door of the Pokémon Gym on Cinnabar Island. It has a red decoration.

items.name: S.S. Ticket
flavor: The ticket required to board the S.S. Anne. It has a drawing of a ship on it.

items.name: Parcel
flavor: A parcel to be delivered to Professor Oak from Viridian City’s Poké Mart.

items.name: Card Key
flavor: A card key that unlocks doors in Silph Co.’s head office in Saffron City.

items.name: Stretchy Spring
flavor: A thin small spring. It’s totally stretched out, and what it’s used for is unknown.

items.name: Chalky Stone
flavor: A small whitish stone picked up at the edge of the road.

items.name: Marble
flavor: A round glass marble. You can see colored glass inside the transparent marble.

items.name: Lone Earring
flavor: A single earring that somebody dropped.

items.name: Beach Glass
flavor: A piece of colored glass. Waves have rounded its edges. It’s slightly rough to the touch.

items.name: Gold Leaf
flavor: A mysterious gold leaf. No trees with this leaf have been found yet.

items.name: Silver Leaf
flavor: A mysterious silver leaf. No trees with this leaf have been found yet.

items.name: Polished Mud Ball

items.name: Tropical Shell
flavor: A beautiful white shell that may have drifted from a sea in a warm region.

items.name: Leaf Letter
flavor: A letter written on a leaf. Something is written using Pikachu’s footprints.

items.name: Leaf Letter

items.name: Small Bouquet

items.name: Lure

items.name: Max Lure

items.name: Pewter Crunchies
